tools.name: update_team_member_role
tools.title: Change Team Member Role
tools.description: Moves an existing collaborator onto a different role within the team. The team owner cannot be re-roled — ownership is not a membership row — and someone who is not in the team is refused. `role` is a role code that must already exist on that team; create it first with `create_role`. Emits `team.member.role_changed`.

user_id.description: UUID of the collaborator whose role is changing.

role.description: Role code to move them onto. Must already exist on the team.

tools.name: update_team
tools.title: Rename Team
tools.description: Renames a team. Owner only — belonging to a team is not enough. Name is the only mutable field; ownership and membership move through their own tools. Emits `team.updated`.

team_id.description: UUID of the team to rename.

tools.name: update_role
tools.title: Update Role
tools.description: Renames a role and replaces its permission set. `permissions` is a REPLACE, not a merge — send the complete list you want the role to end up with, and omit the key entirely to leave the existing set untouched. `code` cannot be changed; permissions are addressed by it, so a rename would detach every assignment. Emits `role.updated`.

role_id.description: UUID of the role to update.

name.description: New role name. Omit to keep the current one.

description.description: New description. Omit to keep the current one.

permissions.description: Complete replacement permission set. Omit to leave permissions untouched.

tools.name: update_group
tools.title: Update Group
tools.description: Renames a group and replaces its permission set. `permissions` is a REPLACE, not a merge — send the complete list, or omit the key to leave the current set alone. `code` cannot change. Membership is untouched here; use `sync_group_members`. Emits `group.updated`.

group_id.description: UUID of the group to update.

name.description: New group name. Omit to keep the current one.

permissions.description: Complete replacement permission set. Omit to leave permissions untouched.

tools.name: sync_group_members
tools.title: Sync Group Members
tools.description: Replaces a group's membership wholesale with the supplied user ids. This is a SYNC, not an add: anyone absent from the list is removed, and an empty array empties the group. Every id must already belong to the group's team — a group grants permissions inside one tenant, so an outsider is refused rather than silently skipped. Emits `group.members_synced`, carrying who was added and who was removed.

group_id.description: UUID of the group whose membership is being replaced.

user_ids.description: Complete list of user UUIDs the group should contain. An empty array clears it.

tools.name: remove_team_member
tools.title: Remove Team Member
tools.description: Removes a collaborator from a team. DESTRUCTIVE: they immediately lose access to every project and setting scoped to it, though their user account itself is untouched. The team owner cannot be removed. To withdraw an invitation nobody has accepted yet, use `cancel_team_invitation` instead — an invitee has no membership row to remove. Emits `team.member.removed`.

user_id.description: UUID of the collaborator to remove.

tools.name: invite_team_member
tools.title: Invite Team Member
tools.description: Invites someone to a team by email and sends them an invitation message. Addressed by email rather than user id because the invitee may have no account yet — that is what separates inviting from adding. `role` is a role code that must already exist on the team; create it first with `create_role`. Someone already in the team is refused. Emits `team.member.invited`, and `team.member.joined` later when they accept.

team_id.description: UUID of the team to invite into.

role.description: Role code the invitee will hold. Must already exist on the team.

tools.name: delete_team
tools.title: Delete Team
tools.description: Permanently deletes a team, owner only. DESTRUCTIVE: everything scoped to the team goes with it — projects, plans, subscriptions, members. There is no restore. The caller's last remaining team is refused, because an account with no tenant is a state no other path can produce. Emits `team.deleted`.

team_id.description: UUID of the team to delete. Irreversible.

tools.name: delete_role
tools.title: Delete Role
tools.description: Deletes a team role and detaches its permissions. DESTRUCTIVE: anyone currently holding this role loses whatever it granted. Restricted to whoever created the role, unless the caller owns the team — belonging to a team is not licence to dismantle how everyone else in it is permissioned. Emits `role.deleted`.

role_id.description: UUID of the role to delete. Irreversible.

tools.name: delete_group
tools.title: Delete Group
tools.description: Deletes a permission group and detaches its permissions and members. DESTRUCTIVE: everyone in the group loses whatever it granted them. The people themselves stay in the team. Emits `group.deleted`.

group_id.description: UUID of the group to delete. Irreversible.

tools.name: create_team
tools.title: Create Team
tools.description: Creates a team owned by the caller. Teams are the tenant every project, plan and subscription hangs off, and are a Growth-tier capability — on a lower tier this returns TEAM_TIER_REQUIRED rather than creating anything. The caller becomes the owner, which is not a membership row and cannot be removed or re-roled. Emits `team.created`.

tools.name: create_role
tools.title: Create Role
tools.description: Creates a permission role inside a team. `code` is the stable identifier permissions are addressed by — it must be unique within the team and cannot be changed afterwards, so choose it deliberately. `permissions` are codes from the permission catalog; read `subscriby://enums/ability` or GET /abilities.json for the accepted list, and note these are the team permission codes (entity:action) rather than token abilities. Growth-tier capability. Emits `role.created`.

team_id.description: UUID of the team the role belongs to.

code.description: Stable identifier, alpha-dash. Unique per team and immutable once created.

description.description: Optional description of what the role is for.

permissions.description: Permission codes (entity:action) to grant. Omit for a role with none.

tools.name: create_group
tools.title: Create Group
tools.description: Creates a permission group inside a team. A group differs from a role in how it is applied: a role is what one collaborator is, a group is a named bundle several people can be put into. `code` is unique per team and immutable. Membership is not set here — use `sync_group_members`, because replacing who is in a group and naming it are separate operations. Growth-tier capability. Emits `group.created`.

team_id.description: UUID of the team the group belongs to.

code.description: Stable identifier, alpha-dash. Unique per team and immutable once created.

tools.name: cancel_team_invitation
tools.title: Cancel Team Invitation
tools.description: Withdraws an invitation nobody has accepted yet, so its link stops working. Distinct from `remove_team_member`: an invitee has no membership row, only a pending invitation, and the two fail on different things. Invitation ids come from the team-members listing.

invitation_id.description: UUID of the pending invitation to withdraw.

tools.name: archive_project
tools.title: Archive Project
tools.description: Archives a project — flips `active` to false so checkout, portal, and bot flows stop accepting new subscribers. Existing subscriptions and payments are untouched. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `project_id` with a human before calling. Idempotent — re-calling on an already-archived project is a no-op. Emits `project.archived` to every subscribed webhook endpoint.

project_id.description: UUID of the project to archive.

tools.name: ban_member
tools.title: Ban Member
tools.description: Bans a project member — flips status to `Banned` and triggers the connector removal pipeline so the subscriber loses access on every linked resource immediately. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `member_id` with a human before calling; banning is socially visible and breaks an active relationship. Idempotent — re-calling on an already-banned member is a no-op. Emits `member.banned`. Use `unban_member` to reverse.

member_id.description: UUID of the project member to ban.

reason.description: Optional human-readable reason that lands in the member.banned event payload.

tools.name: broadcast_message
tools.title: Broadcast Message
tools.description: Sends a message through the project's connector to a segment of its members. DESTRUCTIVE AND IRREVERSIBLE: you MUST show a human the exact message text, the audience segment and the recipient count from `preview_broadcast_audience`, and get explicit approval, before calling. A broadcast cannot be recalled once queued and every recipient is a real person. NOT idempotent — calling twice sends twice. Emits `broadcast.queued` then `broadcast.completed` with sent/failed tallies. Use `preview_broadcast_audience` first, always. Answers with `broadcast_id`: the creator follows the send on the dashboard and in the Copilot, and `get_broadcast` reads its tallies and the members it could not reach.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose members will receive the message.

message.description: The message body, 1-4096 characters. Canonical HTML subset only (<b>, <i>, <u>, <s>, <a>, <code>, <pre>, <blockquote>, <tg-spoiler>); anything else is stripped before sending.

audience.description: Segment to address: all, customer, trialing, lead, churned, expiring_soon, cancelled_still_active, paused, trialing_cardless, waiting_on_connection, all_pass_holders, all_pass_holders_not_in_queue, pass_holders, pass_holders_not_in_queue. Defaults to `all`, which reaches every member with a linked chat.

pass_window_id.description: Required for the single-window pass segments (`pass_holders`, `pass_holders_not_in_queue`); ignored by the others.

plan_id.description: Optional. Narrows the segment to members on one subscription plan, by plan UUID. Composes with the segment rather than replacing it: `customer` plus a plan reaches people paying for that plan right now, `churned` plus a plan reaches people who held it and left. Rejected for `lead` (never subscribed) and for the pass segments (their plan is implied by the window).

expiring_within_days.description: Only meaningful for `expiring_soon`. How many days ahead to look, 1-90, default 7. A member is counted only if their access genuinely lapses: an auto-renewing subscription is not expiring.

tools.name: retry_broadcast
tools.title: Retry Broadcast
tools.description: Sends a finished broadcast again, to the members it could not reach and nobody else, as a new broadcast under the old one. DESTRUCTIVE: every member reached is a real person, so show a human the parent's `failed_count` from `get_broadcast` and get explicit approval before calling. Refused while the parent is still sending, when it missed nobody, or when none of the missed can be reached now. Answers with the child's `broadcast_id`, `parent_id`, `recipient_estimate` and `estimated_seconds`; follow it with `get_broadcast`. Emits `broadcast.queued` then `broadcast.completed`, both carrying `parent_id`.

broadcast_id.description: UUID of the finished broadcast whose missed members are tried again.

tools.name: bulk_generate_access_codes
tools.title: Bulk Generate Access Codes (Async)
tools.description: Queues a batch generation of access codes for a plan. ASYNC — returns a `job_id` immediately; poll `get_job_status` until `status` is `completed` or `failed`. Only one batch per plan may be in flight; queueing a second while the first is unresolved is refused and names the live `job_id`. The response also carries `preview` (`free_remaining`, `chargeable_quantity`, worst-case overage cost) so the agent can surface the charge to a human before queuing; call `preview_access_code_cost` if you need the same numbers without enqueuing the batch. Generation is free — Stripe metered overage triggers on REDEMPTION when the creator-tier free allotment is exhausted. Set `export_type=messages` (with `consent=true`) to deliver one message per code to the creator's connector chat, or `export_type=file` to receive a CSV via the bot. Emits `access_code.generated` once when the worker finishes.

plan_id.description: UUID of the plan to attach the generated codes to.

quantity.description: How many access codes to generate (1-1000).

export_type.description: How the job delivers the codes to the creator — file (CSV via bot) or messages (one per code via bot). Required.

custom_expiry_amount.description: When expiry_preset=custom, the amount of custom_expiry_type units. Required when preset=custom.

custom_expiry_type.description: When expiry_preset=custom, one of days/weeks/months/years. Required when preset=custom.

consent.description: Required and must be true when export_type=messages — acknowledges that one message per code will be sent to the creator's connector chat.

tools.name: cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel Subscription
tools.description: Cancels a subscription. Async — the call queues a provider-side cancellation; the local row flips to `canceled` and `subscription.cancelled` emits when the worker finishes. Returns `{ subscription_id, status: "cancellation_queued" }` immediately. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `subscription_id` with a human before calling — this stops billing and revokes connector resource access on the next sync. Idempotent — already-canceled subscriptions return `SUBSCRIPTION_ALREADY_ACTIVE` rather than double-firing.

subscription_id.description: UUID of the subscription to cancel.

tools.name: complete_creator_task
tools.title: Complete Creator Task
tools.description: Marks a hand-arranged perk as handed over: the task is recorded done by the token's user, the access ledger row moves from `pending` to `granted`, and `creator_task.completed` then `member.resource_added` are raised for the grant. Use it after the creator confirms they handed the perk over — never to tidy the list, because it says the member received something. Read the task back with `list_creator_tasks` first. A task already done, or one whose purchase has ended so there is nothing left to grant, is `VALIDATION_FAILED`; an unknown or out-of-scope `task_id` is `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

task_id.description: UUID of the task to complete, from `list_creator_tasks` or the `creator_task.opened` event.

tools.name: reactivate_subscription
tools.title: Reactivate Subscription
tools.description: Undoes a scheduled cancellation, putting the subscription back on its normal billing cycle. This is the recovery path for a cancellation made in error, and the tool to reach for on a win-back ("they changed their mind"). Refuses a subscription that was never cancelled. Emits `subscription.reactivated`. Safe to call — it restores an intent the member already had.

subscription_id.description: UUID of the subscription to act on.

tools.name: unpause_subscription
tools.title: Unpause Subscription
tools.description: Resumes a paused subscription, restarting billing and restoring resource access. Refuses anything that is not currently paused. Emits `subscription.unpaused`. Safe to call — this restores service rather than removing it.

subscription_id.description: UUID of the subscription to act on.

tools.name: pause_subscription
tools.title: Pause Subscription
tools.description: Pauses an active or trialing subscription: billing stops and the member keeps their place without being cancelled. This is the non-destructive alternative to `cancel_subscription` — prefer it whenever a human asks to "stop billing", "put on hold" or "freeze" an account, because it can be undone with `unpause_subscription` while a cancellation cannot. Confirm the target with a human first; the member loses resource access. Idempotent — pausing an already-paused subscription is a no-op. Emits `subscription.paused`.

subscription_id.description: UUID of the subscription to act on.

tools.name: create_coupon
tools.title: Create Coupon
tools.description: Creates a coupon code on a project — one code any number of subscribers can redeem for money off. Distinct from an access code, which is one code for one person and grants access outright. `code` accepts letters, numbers and dashes only and is stored uppercase. Set `discount_type=percentage` with `discount_value` 1..99, or `discount_type=fixed` with a `currency_id`; a fixed discount only applies to plans priced in that same currency, while a percentage applies to any. Leave `plan_ids` empty to cover EVERY plan in the project, including ones added later. Omit `max_redemptions` for unlimited uses. The discount applies to the FIRST payment only — renewals are charged in full. Coupons require the Growth tier or the Coupons addon; on any other tier the call is rejected. Discounts cannot be honoured on Razorpay at all, nor on recurring plans through any provider except Stripe — the checkout tells the buyer so rather than silently charging full price.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the code belongs to.

code.description: The code subscribers type at checkout. Letters, numbers and dashes only, 3 to 64 characters. Stored uppercase.

name.description: Internal label to tell your codes apart, e.g. "Black Friday 2026". Defaults to the code itself.

discount_type.description: Either "percentage" (works on plans in any currency) or "fixed" (requires currency_id, and only applies to plans priced in it).

discount_value.description: For percentage, 1..99. For fixed, an amount greater than zero in the chosen currency.

currency_id.description: Currency UUID. Required when discount_type is "fixed", ignored otherwise.

max_redemptions.description: Total uses allowed across everyone. Omit for unlimited.

max_redemptions_per_user.description: How many times one subscriber may use the code. Defaults to 1.

minimum_amount.description: Only apply the code when the plan costs at least this much, in the plan's own currency.

starts_at.description: ISO 8601 instant the code becomes usable. Omit to start immediately.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 instant the code stops working. Omit for no end date.

plan_ids.description: Plan UUIDs to restrict the code to. Leave empty or omit to cover every plan in the project, including ones added later.

active.description: Whether the code is usable right away. Defaults to true.

tools.name: create_plan
tools.title: Create Plan
tools.description: Creates a subscription plan on a project. Every plan has a `kind`, and the kind decides which ONE nested object you must send with it: `subscription` takes `billing`, `pass` takes `pass`, `pass_series` takes `pass_series`. Sending a block that does not match the kind is rejected. `currency_id` must be supported by an active payment method on the project. The user-type restriction flags inside `eligibility` (`newcomers_only`, `customers_only`, `churned_only`) are mutually exclusive. Defaults: `kind=subscription`, `active=true`. Emits `plan.created`. KIND subscription: access begins at payment and renews on a cycle; `resources` is required; `billing.billing_cycle=lifetime` requires `billing_cycle_count=1`. KIND pass: sells ONE scheduled access window per purchase; `resources` is required; supply `pass.timezone`, `pass.recurrence` and `pass.slots`, where each slot carries its own `duration_minutes` so one plan can mix a 3-hour and a 14-hour window. KIND pass_series: sells a curated slate of OTHER pass plans' windows for one payment — a season ticket; it owns no windows of its own, so `pass_series.window_ids` must name windows that already exist (use the `list_pass_windows` tool to find them) and `resources` is OPTIONAL, meaning a lounge open for the whole span rather than the thing being sold. Passes and series both require Time-Limited Passes, bundled with Growth or available as the Passes Addon; on any other tier the call is rejected.

project_id.description: UUID of the parent project.

kind.description: subscription (access starts at payment and renews on a cycle), pass (one dated access window per purchase), or pass_series (a season ticket over many of your pass plans' windows). Defaults to subscription. Decides which nested block below is required.

name.description: Plan name (min 5, max 255 chars, unique per project).

currency_id.description: UUID of the currency. Must be supported by an active payment method on the project.

price.description: What one purchase costs, as a decimal. On a pass this buys one window; on a pass_series it buys the whole slate, once. At least the $1.00 USD equivalent — payment providers reject smaller amounts. 0 publishes a free plan and requires the Starter or Growth tier.

resources.description: UUIDs of project_resources this plan grants access to. Required on kind subscription and kind pass. OPTIONAL on kind pass_series, where it means a lounge the holder keeps for the whole span — each pass in a series already grants its own plan's resources.

description.description: Optional plan description. Max 1000 chars, HTML is filtered.

active.description: Defaults to true. Set false to create in draft state.

sales_cap.description: Optional. Pause the plan automatically after this many successful purchases (1-100000); the creator publishes it again for another batch. Omit or null for no limit.

eligibility.description: Audience restrictions: {newcomers_only?: bool, customers_only?: bool, churned_only?: bool, single_use?: bool, access_codes_only?: bool}. The first three are mutually exclusive.

billing.description: REQUIRED when kind=subscription, refused otherwise. {billing_cycle: days|weeks|months|years|lifetime, billing_cycle_count: int 1-99, recurring?: bool, disabled_renewal?: bool, trial_days?: int 0-365, trial_cardless?: bool, trial_type?: string}. lifetime requires billing_cycle_count=1. recurring must be false for crypto / platform currencies.

pass.description: REQUIRED when kind=pass, refused otherwise. {timezone: IANA zone e.g. America/New_York, schedule_mode?: repeating|fixed, recurrence?: daily|weekly|monthly, recurrence_ends_at?: ISO-8601, sales_cutoff_minutes?: int, sales_cutoff_anchor?: before_start|before_end, slots?: array, windows?: array}. Slot times are local wall-clock in `timezone` and survive daylight saving. Each slot is {weekday?: 0-6 with 0=Sunday, day_of_month?: 1-31, start_time: "HH:MM", duration_minutes: int} — each carries its own duration, so a plan can mix lengths, and a day_of_month of 29-31 skips months that lack the day. `windows` places explicit dates for schedule_mode=fixed: {starts_at: "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM", duration_minutes: int}. sales_cutoff_anchor before_start (default) stops sales that many minutes before a window opens; before_end keeps it on sale while it runs, requires at least 1, and must be under the shortest slot duration_minutes.

pass_series.description: REQUIRED when kind=pass_series, refused otherwise. {window_ids: array of pass-window UUIDs, prevent_overlaps?: bool, sales_cutoff_minutes?: int, sales_cutoff_anchor?: before_start|before_first_end|before_last_start|before_end, seat_cap?: int, successor_plan_id?: UUID, presale_hours?: int 1-8760, blackout_window_ids?: array, rules?: array}. A series points at windows that ALREADY EXIST on your pass plans — it never creates any — so get their UUIDs from the `list_pass_windows` tool first. Needs at least two windows, or a rule that will find them. `rules` grows the slate automatically and keeps doing so after holders have bought, granting new matches to them at no charge: each rule is {source_plan_id: UUID of a pass plan, kind: date_range|next_n, from_at?: ISO-8601, to_at?: ISO-8601, take?: int}, where date_range takes every window starting in the period and next_n takes the next `take` windows and then stops. sales_cutoff_anchor before_start closes sales before the FIRST window opens; before_first_end keeps the season on sale into that opening window and closes a set number of minutes (at least 5) before it ends, so a latecomer can still join on the night; before_last_start keeps it on sale until the LAST window opens, so a buyer always gets at least one whole date; before_end keeps the season on sale right through, closing before the LAST window ends. All three sell at full price for whatever remains, and windows that already ran are never issued.

tools.name: create_project
tools.title: Create Project
tools.description: Creates a project owned by the authenticated creator's current team. Enforces creator-tier project limits — exhausted tiers return `TEAM_TIER_REQUIRED`. A project has no platform of its own: install connectors on it afterwards with `install_connector`. `handle` (URL-friendly slug used to build the subscriber portal URL) may be chosen on every tier and is generated when omitted; it can be changed later, and every former handle keeps redirecting to the current one. Emits `project.created`.

description.description: Optional description. Max 1000 chars, HTML is filtered.

handle.description: Optional URL-friendly handle, on every tier. Alpha-dash lowercase, 5-255 chars, unique across every project's current and former handles; omitted, a random one is assigned.

terms.description: Optional URL to the terms page. Max 255 chars.

privacy.description: Optional URL to the privacy page. Max 255 chars.

active.description: Defaults to true. Set false to create in draft state.

hide_branding.description: Take the "Powered by Subscriby" mark off the portal page, its social card and the bot. Defaults to false on every plan; true needs a Starter or Growth tier (TEAM_TIER_REQUIRED otherwise).

team_id.description: Optional UUID of the owning team. Defaults to the token's scoped team.

tools.name: create_resource
tools.title: Create Manual Resource
tools.description: Creates a manual project resource (PDF link, token, URL placeholder, anything that is not a place a connector gates); its `kind` is `manual` and its `connector` and `space` are null. HARD RULE: gated places (a connector's channels, groups or servers) CANNOT be created here — they are linked through the connector with `request_resource_link`, which asks the creator to pick the place inside the platform client so the connector first proves it administers it before the row persists. `title` must be 5..255 chars. Defaults: `active=true`. Emits `project.resource.created`.

project_id.description: UUID of the parent project.

description.description: Optional resource description. Max 1000 chars, HTML is filtered.

active.description: Defaults to true. Set false to create in inactive state.

tools.name: create_resource_from_space
tools.title: Create Resource From Space
tools.description: Sells a place picked from the list a connector offers: creates the resource for it and binds it to the place, the way the connector's own link flow does. `kind` is spelled `connector:kind` on a connector whose directory card declares `space_browsing`, and `external_id` is a place `list_connector_spaces` listed for that kind; the installation is asked again and a place it does not list is `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, so a resource is never bound to a place the installation does not administer. A place the project already sells answers its existing resource. `title` must be 5..255 chars. Emits `project.resource.linked`. A connector that cannot list its places, such as one whose link starts on the platform, takes `request_resource_link` instead; a manual perk takes `create_resource`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the place will belong to.

kind.description: The kind of place, spelled `connector:kind`: a connector's key, a colon, and one of the `resource_kinds` that `list_connectors` lists for it.

external_id.description: The platform's id for the place, as `list_connector_spaces` lists it under `external_id`.

title.description: Resource title (5..255 chars), what members read.

description.description: Optional resource description. Max 1000 chars, HTML is filtered.

tools.name: delete_resource
tools.title: Delete Resource
tools.description: Hard-deletes a project resource by UUID — the row is removed from the database with no soft-delete fallback. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `resource_id` with a human before calling; every plan that links this resource loses the link and existing subscribers may lose access on the next sync. Emits `project.resource.deleted` BEFORE the row disappears so webhook listeners receive the final snapshot. Idempotent — re-calling on an already-deleted id returns `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

resource_id.description: UUID of the resource to delete.

tools.name: find_member_by_identity
tools.title: Find Member by Identity
tools.description: Finds one project member by the account they connected on a connector: `project_id`, the `connector` key (as `list_connectors` lists them) and the platform's own `external_id` for the account (as `list_member_identities` shows it). Answers the same row as `get_subscriber`, with `identities` loaded. PII WARNING: `email` and `billing_email` are returned verbatim — scrub before forwarding to any third-party LLM, log sink, or analytics surface. An unknown project, a connector the project does not run, or an account no member of the project linked is `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the member belongs to.

connector.description: Connector key the account lives on, as `list_connectors` lists them.

external_id.description: The platform's own id for the account, as `list_member_identities` shows it.

tools.name: get_account_export
tools.title: Get Account Export
tools.description: Returns the creator's most recent account export: its `status` (`queued`, `building`, `ready`, `failed` or `expired`), when it was requested and finished, its size and project count, and, while `ready`, a signed `download_url` with `download_url_expires_at`. The same payload as `GET /v1/me/export`. Answers `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` when no export was ever requested. Takes no input.

tools.name: get_activity_log
tools.title: Activity Log
tools.description: Reads the activity log for one subject (project, project-user, plan, etc.) in reverse-chronological order. Pass `subject_type` as a supported alias: `project`, `project-user`, `project-subscription`, `project-subscription-plan`, `member`, `subscription`, `plan`, `access-code`, `coupon`, `project-resource`. Anything else is refused, and a subject belonging to another creator returns RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND rather than its history. Each entry carries causer, event, and properties; keys matching `token|secret|password|api_key|api_secret` are scrubbed before return.

subject_type.description: Alias of the model the activity is attached to: one of project, subscription, project-subscription, member, project-user, plan, project-subscription-plan, access-code, coupon, project-resource, referral-program, referral-affiliate, smart-link, sequence, knowledge-entry. Model class names are refused.

limit.description: Maximum entries to return (1..200, default 50).

tools.name: get_connector
tools.title: Get Connector
tools.description: Reads one Connectors Marketplace card by its `connector` key (such as the value `list_connectors` returned): the lane (`status`), `installable`, `official`, the badges, the category, tagline, overview and links, and for a connector that exists as a package the whole manifest with its `resource_kinds`, `capabilities`, `messaging` limits, `pacing`, `management_commands` and `missing_commands`, `recovery` facets and the declarative `install_fields` and `settings_fields`. A key nobody knows is `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. Use it to answer "what can this connector do?" or "what does connecting it ask the creator for?".

connector.description: The connector key, as `list_connectors` returns it.

tools.name: get_connector_analytics
tools.title: Connector Analytics
tools.description: Returns members, access and revenue per connector for the authenticated creator — one row per connector their projects run or ever granted access on, with the live installations, the members holding a linked account (and how many linked one in the window), the live and pending grants, the grants issued and revoked in the window, the gross revenue in USD with its transaction count and its share of the scope's total. A purchase that grants access on two connectors counts toward both (`attribution` says so). Accepts an optional `project_id`, a `period` preset (`7d`, `14d`, `30d`, `60d`, `90d`, `mtd`, `qtd`, `ytd`, `1y`, `all`) or explicit `from`/`to` ISO dates. Answers "which connector earns, and which one do members actually use?".

project_id.description: Optional project UUID to scope the figures. Leave blank for all projects in the current team.

period.description: Period preset — 7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 90d, mtd, qtd, ytd, 1y, all. Defaults to 30d.

from.description: Explicit start date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Overrides period when paired with "to".

to.description: Explicit end date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Overrides period when paired with "from".

tools.name: get_connector_installation
tools.title: Get Connector Installation
tools.description: The health and connection state of one connector on a project: the bot or app, its state and whether it can act right now. Reads a project's live installation of one connector by `project_id` and `connector` key: the `state` (`pending`, `connected`, `degraded`, `revoked`, `disconnected`) with its reason and detail, whether the creator can fix it (`creator_actionable`), whether it can act right now (`operational`), the platform's own `external_id`, `display_name`, `handle` and `avatar_url`, and the timestamps of its life. `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` with `reason` `unknown_connector` when the key names no connector, `CONNECTOR_NOT_INSTALLED` when the project has no installation of it.

project_id.description: UUID of the project.

connector.description: The connector key, as `list_connectors` returns it.

tools.name: get_connector_uninstall_preview
tools.title: Get Connector Uninstall Preview
tools.description: Shows what uninstalling a connector from a project would touch, changing nothing: the connector's `resources` (deactivated as detached, external ids kept), the `live_grants` on them (revoked, members put outside), the `emptied_plans` left with nothing to grant, the `recurring_subscriptions` on those plans the creator may have cancelled at period end and the `one_time_subscriptions` that are never cancelled, `affected_subscription_ids`, the `upcoming_windows` of emptied pass plans, `open_support_threads` on the connector and `member_identities` that lose their reach. `options` are the two opt-ins with their defaults. Read this and confirm with the creator before calling `uninstall_connector`. `CONNECTOR_NOT_INSTALLED` when the project has no installation of the connector.

project_id.description: UUID of the project.

connector.description: The connector key, as `list_connectors` returns it.

tools.name: get_dashboard_metrics
tools.title: Headline Dashboard Metrics
tools.description: Returns headline dashboard metrics for the authenticated creator: MRR, active subscribers, churn, and a plan-level breakdown, with a comparison-window delta. Accepts a `period` preset (`7d`, `14d`, `30d`, `60d`, `90d`, `mtd`, `qtd`, `ytd`, `1y`, `all`) or explicit `from`/`to` ISO dates. Pair with `get_earnings_report` for the timeseries view and `get_subscriber_analytics` for lifecycle detail. Backed by the same 5-minute cache the dashboard uses, so repeated calls within a window return the same numbers.

project_id.description: Optional project UUID to scope the metrics to. Leave blank for all projects in the current team.

period.description: Period preset — 7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 90d, mtd, qtd, ytd, 1y, all. Defaults to 30d. Ignored when both from and to are supplied.

from.description: Explicit start date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Overrides period when paired with "to".

to.description: Explicit end date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Overrides period when paired with "from".

compare_period.description: Baseline to compare against — "previous" (prior window) or "none". Defaults to "previous".

tools.name: get_deep_link
tools.title: Build Bot Deep Link
tools.description: Builds a shareable deep link into a project's bot on its connector, carrying a `start` payload. Pass `plan_id` (UUID) to pre-select that plan, or `access_code` (UUID) to hand out a one-time redemption link — the bot acts on the raw UUID. `custom` (1–64 chars of A–Za–z0–9_-) is an arbitrary passthrough for external click tracking; the bot itself opens the project home for it. Without any of those, the link opens the bot on the project home flow. Returns `VALIDATION_FAILED` with `reason=no_bot_attached` if the project has no bot connected.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose bot URL to embed in the deep-link.

plan_id.description: Optional plan UUID. When set, the payload is that UUID verbatim and the bot opens the plan checkout.

access_code.description: Optional access-code UUID. When set, payload is the UUID verbatim for one-tap redemption.

custom.description: Optional caller-supplied payload. Useful for campaign / referral tracking.

tools.name: get_earnings_report
tools.title: Earnings Report (Timeseries)
tools.description: Returns a full earnings report for the authenticated creator — totals (gross, fees, net, transactions) plus a day / week / month timeseries via the `granularity` argument. Accepts a `period` preset (`7d`, `14d`, `30d`, `60d`, `90d`, `mtd`, `qtd`, `ytd`, `1y`, `all`) or explicit `from`/`to` ISO dates. Explicit dates win when both are supplied. Pair with `get_dashboard_metrics` for headline KPIs and `get_transaction_breakdown` for per-dimension splits.

project_id.description: Optional project UUID to scope the report. Leave blank for all projects in the current team.

period.description: Period preset — 7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 90d, mtd, qtd, ytd, 1y, all. Defaults to 30d. Ignored when both from and to are supplied.

from.description: Explicit start date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Overrides period when paired with "to".

to.description: Explicit end date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Overrides period when paired with "from".

granularity.description: Timeseries bucket size — day, week, month. Defaults to day.

statuses.description: Optional SubscriptionStatus allow-list applied to parent subscriptions.

payment_method_ids.description: Optional payment-method UUID allow-list applied to parent subscriptions.

tools.name: get_job_status
tools.title: Poll MCP Async Job
tools.description: Polls a long-running MCP job by id and returns its current `status` (`queued`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`) plus the final `result` or `error` once the worker finishes. Always pair with any tool that returns a `job_id` (`bulk_generate_access_codes`, `request_account_export`, and `revert_recovery_operation` for a channel revert); poll until `status=completed`, or in the Copilot watch the step, which follows the job live. Visibility is locked to jobs the authenticated user originally kicked off — foreign job ids return `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` to prevent existence leaks.

job_id.description: UUID of the async job to poll.

tools.name: get_me
tools.title: Get Me
tools.description: Describes the creator this token belongs to: id, name, email, locale, platform plan and its capabilities, the team the token is scoped to (`current_team`, the id the other tools act in) and every team they belong to, the accounts linked on the connectors, and where their alerts go (`alert_destinations`, with `alert_destinations_default` true when no destination was written and every class reaches the primary connected account). Call it first to learn who you are acting as. Takes no input.

tools.name: get_plan_performance
tools.title: Per-Plan Performance
tools.description: Returns one row per plan within a project: active subscribers, payments-in-window, revenue-in-window, and average ticket size. Aggregates across a `period` preset (`7d`, `14d`, `30d`, `60d`, `90d`, `mtd`, `qtd`, `ytd`, `1y`, `all`) or explicit `from`/`to` ISO dates. Use to spot underperforming or breakout plans before reaching for `get_transaction_breakdown` (which pivots on dimensions other than plan).

project_id.description: UUID of the project to report on.

period.description: Period preset — 7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 90d, mtd, qtd, ytd, 1y, all. Defaults to 30d. Ignored when both from and to are supplied.

from.description: Explicit start date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Overrides period when paired with "to".

to.description: Explicit end date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Overrides period when paired with "from".

tools.name: get_revenue_composition
tools.title: Revenue Composition
tools.description: Returns how the window's revenue and payments are composed, as the five donuts the dashboards draw: transaction fees by payment provider, settled transactions by plan kind (subscription, one-time, lifetime, pass), gross revenue by currency in USD, payment attempts by outcome (succeeded, pending, failed), and, unwindowed because it is a balance, the monthly recurring revenue split by plan. Every dataset carries `total`, `unit` (`usd` or `count`) and `slices` sorted largest first, each slice with its `key`, `label`, `value`, `share_percent` and chart `color`. Accepts an optional `project_id`, a `period` preset (`7d`, `14d`, `30d`, `60d`, `90d`, `mtd`, `qtd`, `ytd`, `1y`, `all`) or explicit `from`/`to` ISO dates. Answers "where do the fees go, what sells, in which currency, how many charges fail, and which plans carry the MRR?".

project_id.description: Optional project UUID to scope the figures. Leave blank for all projects in the current team.

period.description: Period preset — 7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 90d, mtd, qtd, ytd, 1y, all. Defaults to 30d. MRR by plan ignores it: it is a balance, not a flow.

from.description: Explicit start date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Overrides period when paired with "to".

to.description: Explicit end date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Overrides period when paired with "from".

tools.name: get_portal_url
tools.title: Build Subscriber Portal URL
tools.description: Builds the subscriber-portal URL for a project: `{frontend_url}/{handle}`. Always reflects the current handle — updating the handle via `update_project` invalidates previously distributed portal URLs. Returns `{ project_id, handle, portal_url }`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose portal URL to return.

tools.name: get_portal_design
tools.title: Get Portal Design
tools.description: Reads a project's portal design: `published`, the document members see, and `draft`, the one being edited or null, each with every key of the fourteen sections (colours, typography, shape, layout, wording, blocks, button and footer, announcement bar, media, sections, behaviour, visibility and code, language) in the stored shape `update_portal_design` takes back, plus `has_draft`, `draft_updated_at`, `published_at` and a preview_url that shows the draft for ten minutes, null until the project has a handle. Requires `project_id`. Unknown or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose portal design to read.

tools.name: get_project
tools.title: Get Project
tools.description: Fetches a single project by UUID, including counts of `plans`, `resources`, `subscribers`, and `payment_methods`. TenantScope enforces that the project belongs to the caller's team — unknown or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (no existence leaks). Pair with `list_projects` to discover the right id first.

project_id.description: UUID of the project to fetch.

tools.name: get_recovery_allowances
tools.title: Get Recovery Allowances
tools.description: Reads how many self-service Disaster Recoveries of each kind (`account`, `bot`, `resources`) the creator this token acts for may still run inside the rolling window, how many uses support has released on top (`grant_remaining`), whether a recovery of that kind would be allowed right now (`allowed`), whether the next one would spend a support grant (`uses_grant`), when the kind was last recovered and when the self-service allowance returns. `meta` carries `window_days` and `self_service_uses`. Answers "can I still run a recovery, or do I need support?". Takes no input.

tools.name: get_recovery_readiness
tools.title: Get Recovery Readiness
tools.description: Reads the Disaster Recovery readiness checklist for the creator this token acts for: every line (the account lines first: a second factor and a backup sign-in account; then each installed connector's own lines, named by `connector`, such as a standby installation, a standby for every gated space, automatic failover and a live mirror; then the reminders: a copy of the content kept elsewhere and a second human administrator) with `done` true, false, or null when the platform can only remind, `locked` when the plan lacks the prevention feature, the state in words (`detail`) and where the fix lives (`url`), plus the totals the dashboard card shows (`completed` of `total`, `complete`, and `prevention` for whether the plan bundles the prevention features). Answers "how ready is this account for the next ban?". Takes no input.

tools.name: get_recovery_roll_call
tools.title: Get Recovery Roll Call
tools.description: Reads where the re-admission after one Disaster Recovery operation stands: how many members the swap set out to re-admit (`total`), how many hold a fresh link into the new space (`regranted`), how many could not be given one (`failed`), how many the installation could not message (`unreachable`) and were told by email instead (`emailed`), how many have joined through their new link (`joined`), who is still outside (`pending`), how many reminders went out (`nudged`), whether the queue has handled everyone (`settled`), and whether the creator may remind the stragglers right now (`can_nudge`, with `nudge_available_at` while the cooldown runs). A recovery of a kind that re-admits nobody answers all zeros. An unknown or another creator's `operation_id` surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

operation_id.description: UUID of the recovery operation, from `list_recovery_operations`.

tools.name: get_recovery_settings
tools.title: Get Recovery Settings
tools.description: Reads one project's Disaster Recovery settings: whether automatic failover is switched on (`auto_failover_enabled`) and when the per-email fee it may charge was accepted, how members are told after a channel swap the creator ran (`email_delivery`: `self` means the creator tells them, `platform` means Subscriby emails them at the per-email fee), and whether a standby installation is kept for the project (`standby_installation_registered`). An unknown or out-of-scope `project_id` surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose recovery settings to read.

tools.name: get_resource
tools.title: Get Resource
tools.description: Fetches a single project resource (a channel, group or server a connector gates, or a manual entry) by UUID. TenantScope enforces that the parent project belongs to the caller's team — unknown or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. Pair with `list_resources` to discover the right id first.

resource_id.description: UUID of the project resource to fetch.

tools.name: get_resource_standby
tools.title: Get Resource Standby
tools.description: Reads the standby kept for one resource: whether it is healthy (`health_status`, with the connector's reason code when degraded), whether every post is mirrored into it (`mirror_enabled`), when it was last probed and last written to, and when it was linked. A resource that keeps no standby, like an unknown or out-of-scope `resource_id`, surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

resource_id.description: UUID of the resource whose standby to read.

tools.name: get_subscriber_analytics
tools.title: Subscriber Analytics
tools.description: Returns subscriber-centric analytics for the authenticated creator — new signups, cancellations, churn rate, trial-to-paid conversion, and a status-distribution snapshot. Accepts a `period` preset (`7d`, `14d`, `30d`, `60d`, `90d`, `mtd`, `qtd`, `ytd`, `1y`, `all`) or explicit `from`/`to` ISO dates. Use to reason about lifecycle health before designing dunning, win-back, or referral campaigns.

project_id.description: Optional project UUID to scope the analytics. Leave blank for all projects in the current team.

period.description: Period preset — 7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 90d, mtd, qtd, ytd, 1y, all. Defaults to 30d.

from.description: Explicit start date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Overrides period when paired with "to".

to.description: Explicit end date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Overrides period when paired with "from".

tools.name: get_support_conversation
tools.title: Get Support Conversation
tools.description: Reads one support conversation with its message history and the member context a reply needs: subscription status, current plan, member-since date and how many messages they have sent. Requires `conversation_id`. `message_limit` caps the history (default 50, max 200, newest last). Internal notes are excluded unless `include_internal` is true, which also requires the support-conversation:update ability — they are private remarks about the member. Attachments are described without their platform file ids, which are credentials. PII WARNING: names, emails and message bodies are returned verbatim.

conversation_id.description: UUID of the support conversation to read.

message_limit.description: How many of the most recent messages to return (1..200, default 50). Returned oldest-first.

include_internal.description: Include creator-only internal notes. Requires the support-conversation:update ability.

tools.name: get_team
tools.title: Get Team
tools.description: Fetches a single team by UUID. Visibility is locked to teams the authenticated user owns or holds a membership in — out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. Pair with `list_teams` to discover the right id first.

team_id.description: UUID of the team to fetch.

tools.name: get_transaction_breakdown
tools.title: Transaction Breakdown by Dimension
tools.description: Splits USD-normalized successful-payment totals by one of `plan`, `payment_provider`, `currency`, or `project` for the requested window. Returns `gross_usd`, `transactions`, and `share_percent` per group. Accepts a `period` preset (`7d`, `14d`, `30d`, `60d`, `90d`, `mtd`, `qtd`, `ytd`, `1y`, `all`) or explicit `from`/`to` ISO dates. Use to answer "where is my revenue concentrated?" — pair with `get_earnings_report` for the timeseries view.

project_id.description: Optional project UUID to scope the breakdown. Leave blank for all projects in the current team.

dimension.description: Required. Grouping dimension — plan, payment_provider, currency, or project.

period.description: Period preset — 7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 90d, mtd, qtd, ytd, 1y, all. Defaults to 30d.

from.description: Explicit start date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Overrides period when paired with "to".

to.description: Explicit end date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Overrides period when paired with "from".

statuses.description: Optional SubscriptionStatus allow-list applied to parent subscriptions.

payment_method_ids.description: Optional payment-method UUID allow-list applied to parent subscriptions.

tools.name: install_connector
tools.title: Install Connector
tools.description: Installs a connector on a project: opens a pending installation with no credentials yet, so the project is marked as running the connector and the creator connects it from the dashboard (connecting needs a credential typed by a person, so no tool does it). Installing a connector that is already installed changes nothing and returns the existing installation. Refuses `CONNECTOR_UNAVAILABLE` for a connector creators may not install today (read `list_connectors`; only `installable` cards qualify) and `CONNECTOR_TIER_REQUIRED` for a second distinct connector on a project whose owner lacks the `multi_connector` capability (Growth). Raises `connector.installed` when a row is opened. Returns the installation as `get_connector_installation` renders it.

project_id.description: UUID of the project.

connector.description: The connector key, as `list_connectors` returns it; only an `installable` card can be installed.

tools.name: kick_member
tools.title: Kick Member
tools.description: Removes a project member without banning them — status rolls to `Churned`, connector resource removal fires through the bot pipeline, and the member can re-subscribe later. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `member_id` with a human before calling; the kick is socially visible and revokes connector access immediately. Emits `member.kicked`. Use `ban_member` instead when re-entry must be blocked.

member_id.description: UUID of the project member to kick.

reason.description: Optional human-readable reason that lands in the member.kicked event payload.

tools.name: list_access_codes
tools.title: List Access Codes
tools.description: Lists access codes attached to a plan. Filter by `status` (`unredeemed`, `redeemed`, `expired`, `all`) and paginate with `limit` (1..100) / `page`. Codes are returned masked (first 4 + last 4 chars) so support staff can match a ticket without the full secret leaving the server. Full code values are only exposed at generation time through `bulk_generate_access_codes`.

plan_id.description: UUID of the plan to list codes for.

status.description: Filter by code state. One of: unredeemed, redeemed, expired, all.

limit.description: Maximum codes to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_connector_installation_actions
tools.title: List Connector Installation Actions
tools.description: Lists what a project's installation of a connector can do for its creator right now, beyond gating: each action with its `key`, the `label` a button would say, a `description` of what will happen, the `fields` the creator fills in first (the same shape as the connector directory's install fields: `name`, `type`, `label`, `help`, `required`, `rules`, `options`) and the "confirm" question to put to the creator before running, when the action needs one (`needs_confirmation`). Empty for a connector that offers none, while the connector is paused, and while the installation cannot act. Run one with `run_connector_installation_action`. Answers "what can Subscriby set up on this server for me?"; `CONNECTOR_NOT_INSTALLED` when the project has no installation of the connector.

project_id.description: UUID of the project.

connector.description: The connector key, as `list_connectors` returns it.

tools.name: list_connector_installations
tools.title: List Connector Installations
tools.description: The health of the connectors on a project: the connection state of each bot or app and whether it can act right now. Lists every connector installation a project holds, oldest first: the `connector` key, the `scope` (`project`, or `platform` for a shared presence Subscriby runs), the `role` (`live` or `standby`), the `state` (`pending`, `connected`, `degraded`, `revoked`, `disconnected`) with its `state_reason` and `state_detail`, whether the creator can fix it (`creator_actionable`), whether it can act right now (`operational`), the platform's own `external_id`, `display_name`, `handle` and `avatar_url`, and when it was connected, verified, revoked, disconnected or uninstalled. Credentials and settings never appear. Answers "which connectors does this project run, and are they healthy?".

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose installations to list.

tools.name: list_connectors
tools.title: List Connectors
tools.description: Lists the Connectors Marketplace: every connector Subscriby knows, lane by lane. Each card carries `status` (`available`, `beta`, `paused` during an incident, `in_development` when built but not yet offered, `coming_soon` for a roadmap entry with no package yet), `installable`, `official`, its `badges` (official or community, new, trending), the category, tagline and overview, the publisher's links and, for a connector that exists as a package, the whole manifest: `install_mode`, `scopes`, the `resource_kinds` it gates (with the grant mode and whether early admission can be held), `capabilities`, `messaging` limits, `pacing`, the `management_commands` its in-chat surface renders and the `missing_commands` it does not, `relay_modes`, the `recovery` facets, and the declarative `install_fields` and `settings_fields` a client renders as the connect form. `status` narrows to one lane. Read this before proposing a connector for a project; the same document is the `subscriby://connectors/catalog` resource.

status.description: Narrow to one lane: `available`, `beta`, `paused`, `in_development` or `coming_soon`. Omit for every lane.

tools.name: list_connector_spaces
tools.title: List Connector Spaces
tools.description: Lists the places of one kind a project's installation of a connector could gate, as the platform lists them right now: the platform's `external_id`, the `kind`, the `title`, the `parent_external_id` on a platform that nests places, and whatever the connector keeps in `meta`. Only a connector that lists its places answers (its directory card declares `space_browsing`); `kind` is one of the connector's `resource_kinds`, as a bare word or spelled `connector:kind`. The list is read from the platform on every call, so a place made a moment ago is on it and a deleted one is not. Pass an `external_id` from here to `create_resource_from_space` to sell the place. Answers "which roles or channels could this project sell?"; `CONNECTOR_NOT_INSTALLED` when the project has no installation of the connector, `CONNECTOR_NOT_CONNECTED` when it cannot act right now, `VALIDATION_FAILED` when the connector lists no places or the kind is not one it gates.

project_id.description: UUID of the project.

connector.description: The connector key, as `list_connectors` returns it; the connector must list its places.

kind.description: The kind of place to list: one of the connector's `resource_kinds`, as a bare word (`role`) or spelled `connector:kind` (`discord:role`).

tools.name: list_coupons
tools.title: List Coupons
tools.description: Lists coupon codes, optionally narrowed to one project via `project_id` or filtered by `active`. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page` (default 1). A coupon is one code many subscribers can redeem for money off — distinct from an access code, which is one code for one person and grants access outright. `plan_ids` empty means the code applies to EVERY plan in the project, not to none. `redemptions.remaining` is derived rather than stored, because an abandoned checkout returns its hold, so prefer it over comparing count against the cap yourself. Use to discover coupon ids before calling `create_coupon` to avoid duplicates.

project_id.description: Optional project UUID to narrow the list to a single project.

active.description: Optional filter: true for codes that are switched on, false for those switched off.

limit.description: Maximum coupons to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_broadcasts
tools.title: List Broadcasts
tools.description: Lists the broadcasts a project sent, newest first, with who sent them and from where, the audience, how far each send got (`progress.line` is the sentence the creator reads) and how many members it could not reach. Narrow with `filter` (`sending` for the ones still moving, `completed`, `failed`) or one exact `status` (`queued`, `sending`, `paused`, `completed`, `failed`). Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page`. History begins with the release that introduced it; older sends have no row. Use `get_broadcast` for one broadcast with the members it missed.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose broadcasts to list.

filter.description: Optional face: `sending` (queued, sending or paused), `completed` or `failed`. Omit for every broadcast.

limit.description: Maximum rows per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_links
tools.title: List Links
tools.description: Lists a project's Smart Links, newest first, each with its slug, its stable code, where it sends people, its three addresses (`urls.web`, `urls.bot`, `urls.embed`), its `state` (`live`, `expired` or `archived`) and its lifetime clicks. Requires `project_id`. Optional `archived` (true for archived links only, false for links still in use, expired ones included) and `search` (name or slug contains). Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page`. A Smart Link is a tracked address a creator hands out per channel; every member who signs in within the attribution window of clicking it is credited to it, which `get_link_funnel` reads. Use to find a link id before `get_link`, `update_link` or `archive_link`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose links to list.

archived.description: Optional: true for archived links only, false for links still in use (expired ones included). Omit for every link.

search.description: Optional: keep links whose name or slug contains this text.

limit.description: Maximum links to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: get_link
tools.title: Get Link
tools.description: Fetches one Smart Link by `project_id` and `link_id`: its name, slug, stable code, destination, the three addresses to share (`urls.web`, `urls.bot`, `urls.embed`), its state and its lifetime clicks. Same row as `list_links`; `get_link_funnel` has the members and the revenue behind it. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the link belongs to.

link_id.description: UUID of the Smart Link to fetch.

tools.name: get_link_funnel
tools.title: Get Link Funnel
tools.description: Reads the Smart Links funnel. With `project_id` alone: every link of the project, live and archived, each with its lifetime clicks, the members it brought (`leads`), those who started a purchase (`checkouts`), those who paid (`paid`), `conversion_rate` (paid per hundred clicks) and `revenue` (everything those members ever paid, per currency and restated in US dollars), plus the `direct` row for the members no link brought and `totals` that equal the project's own figures, so the rows add up. With `link_id` as well: that one link's row. The figures are lifetime by design and count removed members and ended purchases, so two channels compare on everything each ever brought. Needs `project-link:view-any` either way. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose funnel to read.

link_id.description: Optional UUID of one Smart Link; omit for every link with the Direct row and the totals.

tools.name: create_link
tools.title: Create Link
tools.description: Creates a Smart Link on a project: a tracked address for one channel (a video description, a bio, a flyer's QR). Requires `project_id`, `name` (a creator-facing label, 2..120 characters), `slug` (the address segment after `/go/`: 2..32 letters, digits and hyphens, lowercased and unique within the project; `go`, `embed`, `portal`, `bot`, `direct`, `new` and `edit` are reserved) and `destination` (`portal` for the portal home, `plan` for one plan's checkout with `plan_id`, or `bot` for the project's bot). Optional `expires_at` (ISO 8601, in the future) stops the link counting after that moment; omit for never. The answer carries the stable seven-character code and the three addresses to share. Emits `link.created`. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` for a reserved or taken slug or a plan of another project. Smart Links are on every plan, so there is no tier refusal.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the link belongs to.

name.description: A creator-facing label, 2 to 120 characters, e.g. "YouTube description".

slug.description: The address segment after /go/: 2 to 32 letters, digits and hyphens, e.g. "youtube". Lowercased and unique within the project.

destination.description: Where the link sends people: "portal" (the portal home), "plan" (one plan's checkout; send plan_id) or "bot" (the project's bot).

plan_id.description: UUID of the plan a "plan" destination opens. Ignored on the other destinations.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 instant after which the link stops counting and crediting. Omit for never.

tools.name: update_link
tools.title: Update Link
tools.description: Changes a Smart Link; only the arguments present move, the rest keep their stored value. Requires `project_id` and `link_id`. Optional `name` (2..120 characters), `slug` (2..32 letters, digits and hyphens, lowercased, unique within the project; the old address stops answering), `destination` (`portal`, `plan` with `plan_id`, or `bot`), `plan_id` and `expires_at` (ISO 8601 in the future, or an empty string to run until archived). The code never changes, so the bot link, the QR and the attribution cookie keep working after a rename. Emits `link.updated` with the fields that moved. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` for a reserved or taken slug or a plan of another project; an archived link can still be renamed.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the link belongs to.

link_id.description: UUID of the Smart Link to change.

name.description: A new creator-facing label, 2 to 120 characters.

slug.description: A new address segment, 2 to 32 letters, digits and hyphens; the old address stops answering.

destination.description: "portal", "plan" (send plan_id unless one is stored) or "bot".

plan_id.description: UUID of the plan a "plan" destination opens.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 instant after which the link stops counting, or an empty string to run until archived.

tools.name: archive_link
tools.title: Archive Link
tools.description: Archives a Smart Link so it stops counting clicks and crediting members. Requires `project_id` and `link_id`. The address keeps landing on the portal home, so a flyer or a bio that carries it never shows anyone an error, and the members, purchases and revenue the link brought keep their figures in `get_link_funnel`. DESTRUCTIVE in the sense that it cannot be undone: an archived link is never put back in use; make a new one instead. Emits `link.archived` the first time; calling it again on an archived link changes nothing and answers the same row.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the link belongs to.

link_id.description: UUID of the Smart Link to archive.

tools.name: get_retention_settings
tools.title: Get Retention Settings
tools.description: Reads a project's Revenue Recovery settings: `grace_days` (how long a failed renewal keeps the member's access while the payment gateway retries, 0 to 30), the `ladder` that window implies in words, `digest_enabled` (one message a day to the owner, only on a day something happened), "cancel_feedback_enabled" (whether the cancellation screen asks the member why) and the three offers the screen can make: `offer_pause_enabled` (one billing cycle on hold where the gateway can hold the charge), `offer_discount_coupon` (applied to the renewals where the gateway can carry a coupon) and `offer_return_coupon` (handed over on the way out, on every payment method); then the two nurture windows, `checkout_stall_hours` (how long a checkout may stay open with no settled charge before it counts as stalled and the stalled-checkout sequences start, 1 to 24) and `trial_notice_days` (how many days before a trial without a card ends its trial-ending sequences start, 1 to 14). Requires `project_id`. `offers_available` says whether the project owner's plan includes the offers (Growth or the Revenue Recovery Addon); the offer settings are stored on every plan and ignored by the screen without it. The row is created with the defaults on the first read. Read it before `update_retention_settings` to see what stands.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose Revenue Recovery settings to read.

tools.name: update_retention_settings
tools.title: Update Retention Settings
tools.description: Changes a project's Revenue Recovery settings; every argument is optional and the row keeps its stored value for each one left out. Requires `project_id`. Optional: `grace_days` (0 to 30; 0 pauses access at the first failed renewal), `digest_enabled`, "cancel_feedback_enabled", `offer_pause_enabled`, `offer_discount_coupon_id` and `offer_return_coupon_id` (each the UUID of one of the project's own coupons, or null to clear the offer), `checkout_stall_hours` (1 to 24: how long a checkout may stay open with no settled charge before it counts as stalled and the stalled-checkout sequences start) and `trial_notice_days` (1 to 14: how many days before a trial without a card ends its trial-ending sequences start; a shorter trial enrols at its start). The three offer settings are stored on every plan and only read by the cancellation screen when the owner's plan includes the offers (Growth or the Revenue Recovery Addon), which `offers_available` in the answer says. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` for a window out of range or a coupon of another project. Nothing is announced: the settings are the creator's own.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose Revenue Recovery settings to change.

grace_days.description: How many days a failed renewal keeps the member's access while the gateway retries, 0 to 30. 0 pauses access at the failure.

digest_enabled.description: Whether the owner gets one message a day with the failures, reminders, pauses and recoveries, only on a day something happened.

cancel_feedback_enabled.description: Whether the cancellation screen asks the member why before the offer. Off skips straight to the offer.

offer_pause_enabled.description: Whether a cancelling member whose gateway can hold the charge is offered one billing cycle on hold.

offer_discount_coupon_id.description: UUID of one of the project's coupons, applied to a cancelling member's renewals where the gateway can carry it; null for no discount offer.

offer_return_coupon_id.description: UUID of one of the project's coupons, handed to a cancelling member on the way out on every payment method; null for no return coupon.

checkout_stall_hours.description: How many hours a checkout may stay open with no settled charge before it counts as stalled and the stalled-checkout sequences start, 1 to 24.

trial_notice_days.description: How many days before a trial without a card ends its trial-ending sequences start, 1 to 14. A shorter trial enrols at its start.

tools.name: get_retention_stats
tools.title: Get Retention Stats
tools.description: Reads what Revenue Recovery did on a project over a window, the figures the dashboard card shows: `failed_renewals`, `reminders_sent`, `access_paused`, `payments_recovered` with `recovered_usd` (what the settled renewals were worth, restated in US dollars), `access_restored`, `winback_sent` and `won_back` (win-back steps delivered on the churn trigger and members they brought back), `cancellations` with `offers_shown` and `offers_taken`, `reasons` (why members cancelled, the most given first, each with its share in percent), and the nurture block: `leads_arrived`, `leads_nurtured` and `leads_converted` (new leads, the ones a lead sequence took, the ones who bought while it ran), `checkouts_started`, `checkouts_stalled` and `checkouts_recovered` with `checkouts_recovered_usd` (what the charges that finished stalled checkouts were worth, in US dollars), `trials_nurtured` and `trials_saved` (trials without a card a trial-ending sequence took, and the ones whose member paid while it ran). Two figures ignore the window: `in_grace_now` (members who keep access on an unpaid renewal right now) and `paused_now` (members paused for non-payment, waiting for a charge to settle). Requires `project_id`. Optional `period` preset: `7d`, `14d`, `30d` (the default), `60d`, `90d`, `1y`, `mtd`, `qtd`, `ytd` or `all`; an unknown preset is `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Use to judge whether the grace window, the offers, the checkout window or a sequence are earning their keep before changing them.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose Revenue Recovery figures to read.

period.description: Window preset: 7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 90d, 1y, mtd, qtd, ytd or all. Defaults to 30d. The two "right now" figures ignore it.

tools.name: list_cancellation_feedback
tools.title: List Cancellation Feedback
tools.description: Lists the cancellation screens a project's members reached, newest first: the member, the plan they were on, the `reason` they picked, their own words in `feedback`, the offer shown (`offer_shown`: `pause`, `discount` or `return_coupon`) and whether they took it (`offer_taken`), where they answered (`surface`: `portal` or `bot`) and the dates of a pause they took. Requires `project_id`. Optional `reason` (`too_expensive`, `not_using_enough`, `not_enough_content`, `content_not_expected`, `found_another_community`, `not_the_right_fit`, `taking_a_break`, `got_what_i_needed`, `technical_problems`, `signed_up_by_mistake` or `other`) and `surface` keep one kind of record; an unknown word is `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page`. A member who left without reaching the screen (a lapsed card, a connector that banned them) has no record here; `get_retention_stats` has the counts and the shares.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose cancellation screens to list.

reason.description: Optional: keep the records whose member gave this reason, such as "too_expensive" or "other".

surface.description: Optional: "portal" for screens answered on the portal, "bot" for screens answered in a connector chat.

limit.description: Maximum records to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_retention_activity
tools.title: List Retention Activity
tools.description: Lists a project's Revenue Recovery ledger, newest first: one row per notice, offer, feedback and win-back message the programme sent, with the member, the `kind` (`payment_failed_notice`, `grace_reminder`, `grace_final_warning`, `access_suspended`, `access_restored`, `payment_recovered`, `offer_shown`, `offer_taken`, `feedback` or `sequence_step`), the `channel` that carried a notice (`chat` or `email`), when it went out, the coupon and the sequence step behind a win-back message, and, once a charge settled for the member after the row, `converted_at` with the `payment_id` that counted it. Requires `project_id`. Optional `kind` keeps one kind of row; an unknown word is `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page`. This is the ledger every figure of `get_retention_stats` is counted from.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose ledger to list.

kind.description: Optional: keep one kind of row, such as "payment_recovered" or "sequence_step".

limit.description: Maximum rows to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_checkouts
tools.title: List Checkouts
tools.description: Lists the checkouts a project's members started on the portal or in a bot, newest first: the member, the plan they were buying, the rail (`provider`), where they started (`surface`: `portal` or `bot`), the order reference the rail was given, when it started, when the hourly sweep counted it as stalled (`stalled_at`, once the project's checkout window passed with no settled charge) and when a charge finished it (`completed_at` with `payment_id`) or another checkout superseded it (`superseded_at`), summed up as `outcome`: "open", "stalled", "recovered" (a charge settled after it had stalled), "completed" (a charge settled before it could stall) or "superseded" (closed with no charge of its own: the member paid through another checkout, or already held a live membership when the sweep looked). One charge finishes one checkout and brings back one stalled checkout, so a member who tapped Pay three times and paid once has one "completed" and two "superseded". `enrollment_id` names the stalled-checkout sequence passage the stall opened. Requires `project_id`. Optional `stalled` and `recovered` (booleans; "recovered" reads among the stalled rows), `plan_id` and `member_id` narrow the page; a word that is not a boolean or an id that is not a UUID is `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page`. An access code redemption or a free trial start is not a checkout and never appears here; `get_retention_stats` has the counts and what the recovered checkouts were worth.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose checkouts to list.

stalled.description: Optional: true for the checkouts the hourly sweep counted as stalled, false for the ones it never did.

recovered.description: Optional: true for the stalled checkouts a charge finished after all, false for the stalled ones still open.

plan_id.description: Optional: UUID of one plan, to keep the checkouts of that plan.

member_id.description: Optional: UUID of one member, to keep their checkouts.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_sequences
tools.title: List Sequences
tools.description: Lists a project's sequences, newest first, each with its `trigger`, its `active` switch, its `steps` in order (the days each waits, the message with its placeholders unfilled, the coupon it carries) and its `counts` all time: `enrolled`, `open` (still receiving steps), `completed` and `won_back` (a payment settled while the member was enrolled: a member won back on a churn sequence, a conversion on the others). Requires `project_id`. Optional `active` (true for running sequences, false for paused ones) and `trigger` (`churned`, `lead`, `stalled_checkout` or `trial_ending`). Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page`. A sequence is the ordered set of messages a member receives on the days the creator chose after one of four moments (they left, they arrived as a lead, their checkout stalled, their trial is about to end), each with the way to the plan as a button. Use to find a sequence id before `get_sequence`, `update_sequence`, `delete_sequence` or `list_sequence_enrollments`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose sequences to list.

active.description: Optional: true for running sequences only, false for paused ones only. Omit for both.

trigger.description: Optional: keep the sequences on one trigger, such as "churned".

limit.description: Maximum sequences to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: get_sequence
tools.title: Get Sequence
tools.description: Fetches one sequence by `project_id` and `sequence_id`: its name, `trigger`, `active` switch, `steps` in order (each with its stable `id`, `position`, `delay_days`, `body` with the placeholders `{name}`, `{project}`, `{coupon}`, `{discount}` and `{link}` unfilled, and the coupon it carries) and `counts` all time (`enrolled`, `open`, `completed`, `won_back`). Same row as `list_sequences`; `list_sequence_enrollments` has the members behind the counts. A sequence of another project, or one the creator deleted, is `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the sequence belongs to.

sequence_id.description: UUID of the sequence to fetch.

tools.name: create_sequence
tools.title: Create Sequence
tools.description: Builds a sequence on a project: the ordered messages a member receives on the days the creator chose after one of four moments, each with the way to the plan as a button. Requires `project_id` and `name` (1..120 characters).
