Optional `trigger`: `churned` (their last live membership ended; the default), `lead` (they arrived without buying), `stalled_checkout` (a checkout they started stayed open past the project's checkout window) or `trial_ending` (a trial without a card is about to end, the project's trial reminder before it); `active` (defaults to true) and `steps`, a list of up to 8 objects in the order they go out, each with `delay_days` (0..180 for the first step, counted from the trigger, 0 meaning the next hourly run; 1..180 for the rest, counted from the step before), `body` (1..1,000 characters; `{name}`, `{project}`, `{coupon}`, `{discount}` and `{link}` are filled per member when the step goes out) and an optional `coupon_id` (one of the project's coupons). The row and its steps are written together, so a refused step leaves no sequence behind; a sequence built without steps exists and enrols nobody until it has one. Emits `sequence.created` once, with the steps. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` when the project owner's plan lacks sequences (Growth or the Revenue Recovery Addon), for an unknown trigger, a step out of bounds or a coupon of another project.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the sequence belongs to.

name.description: A creator-facing label, 1 to 120 characters, e.g. "Win-back after churn".

trigger.description: What enrols a member: "churned" (their last live membership ended; the default), "lead" (they arrived without buying), "stalled_checkout" (a checkout they started stayed open past the window the project set) or "trial_ending" (a trial without a card is about to end).

active.description: Whether the sequence enrols and sends from the start. Defaults to true.

steps.description: The steps in the order they go out, at most 8: each {delay_days: int, 0-180 on the first step and 1-180 after, body: string up to 1,000 characters with {name}, {project}, {coupon}, {discount} and {link} as placeholders, coupon_id?: UUID of one of the project's coupons}. Omit for a sequence with no steps yet.

tools.name: update_sequence
tools.title: Update Sequence
tools.description: Changes a sequence; only the arguments present move. Requires `project_id` and `sequence_id`. Optional `name` (1..120 characters), `trigger` (`churned`, `lead`, `stalled_checkout` or `trial_ending`; members already part-way through keep their passage), `active` and `steps`. `steps`, when present, replaces the whole list in order (at most 8, each {delay_days 0..180 on the first step and 1..180 after, body up to 1,000 characters, optional coupon_id}): a step still at its place keeps its id and a member due it keeps their position, the rest are appended and the extra ones removed from the end; an empty list removes every step. Switching `active` off is DESTRUCTIVE in the sense that every member part-way through leaves the sequence at once (`sequence.exited` with the reason "disabled") and nobody is enrolled until it runs again; switching it back on enrols nobody retroactively. Emits `sequence.updated` once, with the sequence as it then stands. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` when the owner's plan lacks sequences, for an unknown trigger, a step out of bounds or a coupon of another project.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the sequence belongs to.

sequence_id.description: UUID of the sequence to change.

name.description: A new creator-facing label, 1 to 120 characters.

trigger.description: What enrols a member: "churned", "lead", "stalled_checkout" or "trial_ending". Members already part-way through keep their passage.

active.description: Switch the sequence on or off. Off lets every member part-way through go and enrols nobody until it runs again.

steps.description: The whole list of steps in order, at most 8, replacing the stored list: each {delay_days: int, 0-180 on the first step and 1-180 after, body: string up to 1,000 characters, coupon_id?: UUID}. A step still at its place keeps its id. Omit to leave the steps alone; send an empty list to remove them all.

tools.name: delete_sequence
tools.title: Delete Sequence
tools.description: Deletes a sequence: every member part-way through leaves it at once (`sequence.exited` with the reason "deleted"), the row and its history stay for the figures, and the id stops answering. Requires `project_id` and `sequence_id`. DESTRUCTIVE and never undone: build a new sequence instead. Emits `sequence.deleted`; a second call on the same id is `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. To stop a sequence without losing it, set `active` to false with `update_sequence`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the sequence belongs to.

sequence_id.description: UUID of the sequence to delete.

tools.name: list_sequence_enrollments
tools.title: List Sequence Enrollments
tools.description: Lists the passages members made through one sequence, the newest first: the member, when they entered, the step due next (`next_position`, `next_due_at`) while the passage is open, and how it ended if it has: `state` is "open", "completed" (every step received) or "exited", and an exited passage says why in "exit_reason": "reactivated" (a charge settled for the member: a member won back on a churn sequence, a conversion on a lead, checkout or trial one), "opted_out" (the platform could not reach them, or they pressed Stop), "disabled" (the sequence was switched off) or "deleted". Requires `project_id` and `sequence_id`. Optional "exit_reason" keeps the passages that ended one way; an unknown word is `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page`. The counts on `get_sequence` are these rows added up.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the sequence belongs to.

sequence_id.description: UUID of the sequence whose passages to list.

exit_reason.description: Optional: keep the passages that ended this way: "reactivated", "opted_out", "disabled" or "deleted". Omit for every passage, open ones included.

limit.description: Maximum passages to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_creator_tasks
tools.title: List Creator Tasks
tools.description: Lists the hand-arranged perks a creator still has to hand over in one project — one task per subscriber and manual resource, with the grant it fulfils, the purchase, the member, the resource title, the instructions and when it is due. A manual resource is a perk no connector can give (a file, a call, a seat somewhere no bot manages), so the purchase's grant waits as a task until the creator marks it done with `complete_creator_task`. `status` is `open` by default (not yet done, purchase still standing), `completed`, or `all`; pages oldest first so the longest-waiting member is at the top, with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page`. Answers "who is still waiting for something I hand over myself?". An unknown or out-of-scope `project_id` surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose tasks to list.

status.description: Which tasks: `open` (default: not yet done, purchase still standing), `completed`, or `all`.

limit.description: Tasks per page (1..100, default 25).

tools.name: list_groups
tools.title: List Groups
tools.description: Lists groups across every team the authenticated user owns or holds a membership in. Groups cluster users for organization but carry no permission payload of their own — lighter-weight than roles. Pair with `list_roles` when reasoning about authorization.

tools.name: list_member_identities
tools.title: List Member Identities
tools.description: Lists the connector accounts a project member has connected: the platform (`connector`), the account's `external_id`, `display_name` and `username`, how the link was proven (`source`: `bot`, `portal`, `handshake`, `adopted` or `backfill`) and which one the project reaches first (`preferred`). Members connect accounts themselves, from the portal or by talking to the project's bot; there is no tool to connect one for them. PII WARNING: external ids and names are returned verbatim — scrub before forwarding to any third-party LLM, log sink, or analytics surface.

member_id.description: UUID of the project member whose connected accounts to list.

tools.name: list_notifications
tools.title: List Notifications
tools.description: Lists the notification centre of the creator this token acts for: every alert the platform sent them (a sale, a support backlog, a bot or channel that went silent, a billing or security notice, a pass window, an onboarding nudge), newest first, each with its `class`, `title`, `body`, where it points (`route` + `params` for a client that maps screens, `url` for one that does not) and whether it was read. `unread` narrows to what they have not opened (`true`) or already have (`false`); `class` narrows to one class (`sales`, `support`, `recovery`, `billing`, `security`, `passes`, `onboarding`); `query` to entries whose title or body contains the words; `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page` page it. Answers "what has happened on my account that I have not looked at?". Mark an entry read with `mark_notification_read`, or everything with `mark_all_notifications_read`.

unread.description: `true` for entries not yet read, `false` for entries already read; omit for every entry.

class.description: One class of alert, or omit for every class.

query.description: Words a title or body must contain; omit for every entry.

limit.description: Entries per page (1..100, default 25).

tools.name: list_pass_windows
tools.title: List Pass Windows
tools.description: Lists the dated access windows a time-limited pass plan generates, with their UUIDs. Narrow with `plan_id` (one pass plan) or `project_id` (every pass plan on a project), and with `status` (scheduled, open, closed, canceled) or `from`/`to` ISO-8601 bounds. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 50) and `page`. Each row carries the window id, the plan it belongs to, its start and end in UTC plus the plan's authoring timezone, its status, whether it is currently on sale, and how many purchases hold it. THIS IS THE TOOL THAT MAKES A PASS SERIES AUTHORABLE: `create_plan` with kind=pass_series takes `pass_series.window_ids`, and a series points at windows that already exist rather than creating any, so their UUIDs have to come from here first. Also useful for reconciling a schedule into an external calendar, or checking what is still sellable before pointing a customer at a plan.

plan_id.description: UUID of one time-limited pass plan. Takes precedence over project_id.

project_id.description: UUID of a project, to list windows across every pass plan on it.

status.description: Filter by lifecycle state: scheduled (not yet open), open (running now), closed (finished), canceled.

from.description: Only windows starting at or after this ISO-8601 timestamp.

to.description: Only windows starting at or before this ISO-8601 timestamp.

limit.description: Maximum windows to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_payment_methods
tools.title: List Payment Methods
tools.description: Lists configured payment methods for one project. Provider secrets, webhook signing secrets, and Stripe Connect account ids are always stripped — only `id`, `provider`, `connector`, `mode`, `active`, and `created_at` are surfaced. `provider` is a gateway code or a `connector:provider` key for a currency a connector brings, and `connector` names that connector or is null. Set `active_only=true` to omit deactivated methods. Safe to call when deciding whether a plan can charge against a given provider.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose payment methods to list.

active_only.description: When true, omits deactivated payment methods.

tools.name: list_plans
tools.title: List Plans
tools.description: Lists subscription plans, optionally narrowed to one project via `project_id`. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page` (default 1). Every row carries a `kind` — subscription, pass or pass_series — and that kind names the ONE nested block accompanying it: `billing` (cycle, trial, renewal), `pass` (timezone, recurrence, sales cutoff, next sellable window) or `pass_series` (span, window count, seats, successor). The other two are absent, so a billing cycle never appears on a plan where the cycle means nothing. Every row also carries `cadence`, the human-readable duration string the portal and bot show. Use to discover plan ids before calling `get_plan_performance`, `list_access_codes`, `bulk_generate_access_codes`, `cancel_subscription`, or `list_pass_windows`.

project_id.description: Optional project UUID to narrow the list to a single project.

limit.description: Maximum plans to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_projects
tools.title: List Projects
tools.description: Lists every project the token's frozen team can access, ordered by `created_at` descending. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page` (default 1). The starting point for most flows — use to discover project ids before calling any other tool that takes a `project_id`.

limit.description: Maximum projects to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_recent_payments
tools.title: Recent Payments
tools.description: Lists the most recent subscription payments for one project, ordered by `occurred_at` descending. Filter by `status` (`successful`, `pending`, `failed`, `refunded`, etc. — see `subscriby://enums/subscription-status`) and cap with `limit` (1..200, default 50). Rows include the external provider id and event id but never the raw webhook payload. Use for live activity feeds; reach for `list_transactions` when you need keyset pagination over a long window.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose payments to list.

status.description: Payment status filter. One of: successful, failed, pending, refunded

limit.description: Maximum payments to return (1..200, default 50).

tools.name: list_recovery_incidents
tools.title: List Recovery Incidents
tools.description: What is wrong right now with a connector, a bot or app, or a place it gates, as the health probes found it. Lists the Disaster Recovery incidents of the creator this token acts for: every problem the health probes detected with the creator's sign-in account (`kind` account), a project's installation (`bot`) or a space it sells (`resources`), with the connector, the project and resource it names, the reason as the connector's code and in words (`reason_label`, `reason_explanation`), when it was detected and, once healed or fixed, when and by which operation it was resolved. `status` is `open` by default (what still needs attention), `resolved`, or `all`; pages newest first with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page`. Answers "is anything of mine banned or broken right now?".

status.description: Which incidents: `open` (default: still needing attention), `resolved`, or `all`.

limit.description: Incidents per page (1..100, default 25).

tools.name: list_recovery_operations
tools.title: List Recovery Operations
tools.description: Lists the Disaster Recovery operations of the creator this token acts for: every recovery ever run, by the creator, by the platform (`automatic`) or on demand, with its kind (`account`, `bot`, `resources`), its state (`started`, `completed`, `failed`, `reverted`), the connector and project, when it started and finished, the failure reason when it failed, and its undo state: `revertible` for whether it can still be undone right now and `revert_window_ends_at` for when that closes. Optional `kind` and `status` narrow the list; pages newest first with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page`. Answers "what has recovery done for me, and can I still undo it?".

kind.description: Only recoveries of this kind: `account`, `bot` or `resources`. Omit for every kind.

status.description: Only operations in this state: `started`, `completed`, `failed` or `reverted`. Omit for every state.

limit.description: Operations per page (1..100, default 25).

tools.name: list_resources
tools.title: List Resources
tools.description: Lists resources attached to one project (the places a connector gates, plus manual perks) ordered by `created_at` descending. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page`; narrows with `kind` (`manual`, or a connector's kind spelled `connector:kind` as `list_connectors` lists each connector's `resource_kinds`) and `connector` (a connector key). Each row carries `kind`, `connector` (null for a manual perk) and `space` (`{id, external_id, title}` when linked, `null` for a perk or an unlinked placeholder). Use to discover resource ids before calling `get_resource`, `unlink_resource`, or `delete_resource`.

project_id.description: UUID of the parent project.

limit.description: Maximum resources to return per page (1..100).

kind.description: Only resources of one kind: `manual`, or a connector's kind spelled `connector:kind` as `list_connectors` lists each connector's `resource_kinds`.

connector.description: Only the resources one connector gates, by the key `list_connectors` lists it under.

tools.name: mark_all_notifications_read
tools.title: Mark All Notifications Read
tools.description: Marks every unread entry of the creator's notification centre as read in one call and answers how many it marked (`marked`). Idempotent: a second call marks nothing and answers `0`. Use it when the creator has caught up; to mark one entry use `mark_notification_read`. Takes no input.

tools.name: mark_notification_read
tools.title: Mark Notification Read
tools.description: Marks one entry of the creator's notification centre as read, so the dashboard bell stops counting it. Idempotent: an entry already read keeps its first `read_at`. Takes the `notification_id` from `list_notifications`; an id that is not one of this creator's entries is `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. To clear the whole backlog use `mark_all_notifications_read`.

notification_id.description: UUID of the entry to mark read, from `list_notifications`.

tools.name: notify_members_of_recovery
tools.title: Notify Members Of Recovery
tools.description: Emails every member the project can reach by email that its bot changed after a bot replacement, with the new bot's link and the portal, at the per-email fee added to the creator's transaction fees. Sent once per recovery: a second call answers with the count already sent and sends nothing. Use it after a bot replacement when members must be told; it spends money and reaches real people, so confirm with the creator first. A recovery that belongs to no project, or a teammate, is `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Returns how many members were `notified`, now or earlier.

operation_id.description: UUID of the bot recovery whose project members to email.

tools.name: nudge_pending_readmissions
tools.title: Nudge Pending Readmissions
tools.description: Sends one reminder, with a fresh link, to every member a channel recovery re-admitted who has not joined the new chat yet, and records the nudge on the operation. Read `get_recovery_roll_call` first: `can_nudge` says whether anyone is still outside and the cooldown has passed. Nobody waiting, a nudge too soon, a recovery of another kind or not the creator's own is `VALIDATION_FAILED` with the reason. Every reminder reaches a real person, so do not loop it. Returns how many reminders were queued.

operation_id.description: UUID of the completed channel recovery whose stragglers to remind.

tools.name: remove_resource_standby
tools.title: Remove Resource Standby
tools.description: Stops keeping a standby for one resource: the standby row is forgotten and mirroring into it stops. The chat itself is untouched on the connector, and the resource keeps pointing at its live chat. Automatic failover can no longer swap this resource until a new standby is linked. Only the project owner may do this; a refusal is `VALIDATION_FAILED`. A resource with no standby succeeds with nothing to remove.

resource_id.description: UUID of the resource whose standby to remove.

tools.name: remove_standby_installation
tools.title: Remove Standby Installation
tools.description: Stops keeping the standby installation (the spare bot) registered for one project and withdraws it from the connector, so the next bot replacement will need a fresh credential pasted on the dashboard. Nothing else changes: the live installation, members and access stay as they are. Only the project owner may do this; a refusal is `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Registering a standby is not offered to tokens, because it takes a credential.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose standby installation to remove.

tools.name: request_account_export
tools.title: Request Account Export (Async)
tools.description: Queues an archive of everything the creator's account holds: the account as `get_me` describes it, the webhook endpoints, the platform subscription with its invoices, and for every project the plans, resources, payment methods, members, subscriptions, payments, coupons, dated windows and support conversations, as JSON files in the REST API's shapes plus one workbook per project. ASYNC — returns an `export_id` and a `job_id` immediately; poll `get_job_status` until `status` is `completed`, then call `get_account_export` for the signed `download_url`, which lives a limited time. One export may be in flight per account and one may be requested a day; a refusal is `VALIDATION_FAILED` and says when the next is allowed. Takes no input. Emits no event.

tools.name: request_resource_link
tools.title: Request Resource Link
tools.description: Asks the creator, through the connector, to pick the place a new resource of a project will be: a kind of place the connector gates, spelled `connector:kind` as `list_connectors` lists each connector's `resource_kinds`. The connector messages them with a picker and the resource appears the moment they choose; nothing is created by this call itself. A project running no connected connector is `CONNECTOR_NOT_INSTALLED`; a creator with no account linked on the connector is `IDENTITY_NOT_LINKED`; a kind no connected connector gates, or a linked account nothing can message right now, is `VALIDATION_FAILED` with the reason. A manual perk is created with `create_resource` instead.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the linked place will belong to.

kind.description: The kind of place to ask for, spelled `connector:kind`: a connector's key, a colon, and one of the `resource_kinds` that `list_connectors` lists for it.

tools.name: request_resource_replacement
tools.title: Request Resource Replacement
tools.description: Asks the creator, through the connector, to pick the chat that replaces one resource's: the bot messages them with a picker, and the swap runs the moment they choose — old links revoked, every active member re-admitted, a recovery operation recorded. Nothing is swapped by this call itself. For a degraded resource the swap will spend the channel recovery allowance (or join the recovery already absorbing swaps); for a healthy one it is on demand and free. A resource that is a perk rather than a place, a creator the bot cannot reach, or a spent quota with no recovery to join is `VALIDATION_FAILED` with the reason. Withdraw an unanswered request with `withdraw_resource_replacement_request`.

resource_id.description: UUID of the resource whose chat should be replaced.

tools.name: request_resource_standby
tools.title: Request Resource Standby
tools.description: Asks the creator, through the connector, to pick the chat that becomes the standby for one resource: the bot messages them with a picker, and the standby is linked the moment they choose. Nothing is linked by this call itself. Needs the Growth Plan and the project owner; a resource that is a perk rather than a place, or a creator the bot cannot reach, is `VALIDATION_FAILED` with the reason. Withdraw an unanswered request with `withdraw_resource_standby_request`.

resource_id.description: UUID of the resource that should get a standby.

tools.name: restore_connector_access
tools.title: Restore Connector Access
tools.description: Brings a project's detached places on a reinstalled connector back: asks the connector about every resource the uninstall detached, reactivates the ones it still controls, and hands every live purchase of a plan granting them fresh access (`member.resource_added` per grant issued). Places the connector no longer controls stay detached for `run_connector_doctor` to explain; plans taken off sale stay off sale. Refused with `CONNECTOR_NOT_CONNECTED` until the installation is connected again. Runs the same action as `POST /v1/projects/{project}/connectors/{key}/installation/restore-access`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project.

connector.description: The connector key, as `list_connectors` returns it.

tools.name: revert_recovery_operation
tools.title: Revert Recovery Operation
tools.description: Undoes a completed Disaster Recovery inside its window (24 hours from completion by default). A channel recovery is undone one swap at a time: name the `resource_id` to put back on its old chat, and every active member is re-admitted there again. An account relink is undone whole, moving sign-in back to the previous account, signing the creator out everywhere and opening a disputed-relink incident for support; name no `resource_id`. A bot replacement cannot be undone. Only the creator who ran the recovery may undo it; a closed window, a swap already put back or a teammate is `VALIDATION_FAILED` with the reason. Returns the operation with its undo state updated; a channel revert also returns a `job_id`, because the members are re-admitted in the background: follow it with `get_job_status`, or in the Copilot the step counts them as they go.

operation_id.description: UUID of the completed recovery to undo, from `list_recovery_operations`.

resource_id.description: For a channel recovery: UUID of the resource to put back on its old chat. Omit for an account relink.

tools.name: run_connector_doctor
tools.title: Run Connector Doctor
tools.description: The health check for a connector on a project: what is wrong with the connection and with each place it gates, with the fix for each. Runs the connector doctor on a project's installation of a connector: verifies the installation (recording its state exactly as `verify_connector_installation` does) and asks the connector about every resource it gates, answering one report with a finding per check — the installation first, then each resource — each with a `severity` (`ok`, `warning`, `critical`), the connector's own `state` word and sentence, whether the creator can fix it and where. `healthy` is true when every finding passed. The report is kept on the installation and raises `connector.doctor_completed` only when the findings differ from the previous run's. Answers "is this connector fully working for the project, and if not, where exactly does it hurt?"; `CONNECTOR_NOT_INSTALLED` when the project has no installation of the connector.

project_id.description: UUID of the project.

connector.description: The connector key, as `list_connectors` returns it.

tools.name: run_connector_installation_action
tools.title: Run Connector Installation Action
tools.description: Runs one action a project's installation of a connector offers, on the platform: `action` is a `key` from `list_connector_installation_actions` and `fields` an object keyed by the names that action declares, each answer checked against the field's rules (`VALIDATION_FAILED` names the field). The answer says what happened in the creator's words: `done` true with a `message` and whatever the connector reports in `details`, or `done` false with the reason and, when the platform refused, the classified `failure`. This changes the platform itself (it may create channels, roles or categories), so when the action lists a "confirm" question, put it to the creator and run only on their yes. `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` when the installation offers no action by that key, `CONNECTOR_NOT_INSTALLED` when the project has no installation of the connector, `CONNECTOR_NOT_CONNECTED` when it cannot act right now.

project_id.description: UUID of the project.

connector.description: The connector key, as `list_connectors` returns it.

action.description: The action key, as `list_connector_installation_actions` lists it.

fields.description: The creator's answers, keyed by the field names the action declares; omit for an action that asks nothing.

tools.name: set_resource_standby_mirror
tools.title: Set Resource Standby Mirror
tools.description: Switches the live mirror into one resource's standby on or off: when on, every post made in the channel is copied into the standby as it is made, so a failover lands members in a channel that already holds the content. Only a channel can be mirrored (a group cannot), the resource must keep a standby, switching on needs the Growth Plan, and only the project owner may do it; a refusal is `VALIDATION_FAILED` with the reason. Returns the standby as it now stands.

resource_id.description: UUID of the resource whose standby to mirror into.

mirror.description: True to copy every post into the standby as it is made, false to stop.

tools.name: update_recovery_settings
tools.title: Update Recovery Settings
tools.description: Changes one project's Disaster Recovery settings; fields left out keep their value. `auto_failover` switches automatic failover on or off — switching it on needs `accepts_email_fee: true` in the same call, because a failover may email the members the bot cannot reach at a per-email fee the creator must agree to, and the Growth Plan. `email_delivery` says how members are told after a channel swap the creator ran: `self` (the creator tells them) or `platform` (Subscriby emails them at the per-email fee). Only the project owner may change these; a refusal is `VALIDATION_FAILED` with the reason. Returns the settings as they now stand.

project_id.description: UUID of the project.

auto_failover.description: Switch automatic failover on (true) or off (false). Omit to leave it.

accepts_email_fee.description: Required true when switching failover on: the creator accepts the per-email fee a failover may charge.

email_delivery.description: How members are told after a swap the creator ran: `self` or `platform`. Omit to leave it.

tools.name: uninstall_connector
tools.title: Uninstall Connector
tools.description: Uninstalls a connector from a project. Distinct from disconnecting and never a deletion: every live grant on the connector's resources is revoked (members are put outside, `member.resource_removed` per grant), its resources are deactivated as detached with their external ids kept, the installation row stays with `uninstalled_at`, identities are never removed, and no money moves by itself. Two opt-ins, both on by default, act on the plans left with nothing to grant: "unpublish_emptied_plans" takes them off sale, "cancel_recurring_subscriptions" cancels their live recurring subscriptions at the end of the paid period and emails each member. One-time and lifetime purchases are never cancelled. Raises `connector.uninstalled` with the counts. Always read `get_connector_uninstall_preview` and confirm with the creator first. `CONNECTOR_NOT_INSTALLED` when the project has no installation of the connector.

project_id.description: UUID of the project.

connector.description: The connector key, as `list_connectors` returns it.

unpublish_emptied_plans.description: Take the plans left with nothing to grant off sale. Default true.

cancel_recurring_subscriptions.description: Cancel the live recurring subscriptions on those plans at the end of their paid period and email each member. Default true. One-time purchases are never cancelled.

tools.name: update_connector_installation_settings
tools.title: Update Connector Installation Settings
tools.description: Changes a project's connector installation settings and capability switches. `settings` is an object keyed by the field names the connector declares in its `settings_fields` (read them with `get_connector`); every declared rule runs, a key the connector never declared is `VALIDATION_FAILED`, and fields left out keep their value. `capabilities` is an object keyed by capability (`messaging`, `broadcasts`, `support_relay`, `native_payments`, `recovery_*`) to true or false; a capability the connector does not declare, or one that cannot be switched off (`access_control`, `management_surface`, `portal_login`, `creator_registration`, `early_admission_hold`), is `VALIDATION_FAILED`. At least one of the two is required. Raises `connector.settings_updated` naming the fields and switches that changed (never a value), only when something did.

project_id.description: UUID of the project.

connector.description: The connector key, as `list_connectors` returns it.

settings.description: The fields to change, keyed by the names the connector declares in `settings_fields`; fields left out keep their value. Optional when `capabilities` is given.

capabilities.description: Capability switches to change, keyed by capability value (`messaging`, `broadcasts`, `support_relay`, `native_payments`, `recovery_*`) to true or false; switches left out keep their value. Optional when `settings` is given.

tools.name: use_resource_standby
tools.title: Use Resource Standby
tools.description: Swaps one resource onto its standby right now, in one click: the resource points at the standby chat, the old invite links are revoked, every active member is re-admitted into the standby, and the standby is consumed. A recovery operation records it; when the resource is healthy and has no open incident the swap is on demand and spends no allowance, otherwise it spends (or joins) the channel recovery allowance. Undo is offered for 24 hours through `revert_recovery_operation`. Only the project owner may do this; no healthy standby, a spent quota or a teammate is `VALIDATION_FAILED`.

resource_id.description: UUID of the resource to swap onto its standby.

tools.name: verify_connector_installation
tools.title: Verify Connector Installation
tools.description: A fresh health probe of the connection a connector holds on a project. Asks the connector whether a project's installation still answers and records the verdict on it: `state` becomes `connected`, `degraded` (with `state_reason`, `state_detail` and `creator_actionable`) or `revoked`, and `health_checked_at` is stamped. A `pending` installation has nothing to verify and is returned as it is. Raises `connector.status_changed` only when the state moved. Answers "is this connector still working for the project?" with a fresh probe rather than the hourly one; `CONNECTOR_NOT_INSTALLED` when the project has no installation of the connector.

project_id.description: UUID of the project.

connector.description: The connector key, as `list_connectors` returns it.

tools.name: withdraw_resource_replacement_request
tools.title: Withdraw Resource Replacement Request
tools.description: Takes back the replacement request the creator has open on the connector, so the picker the bot sent stops waiting for an answer. A creator holds one such request at a time, so there is nothing to name; when none is open the call changes nothing and still succeeds. Only the account holder may do this. Takes no input.

tools.name: withdraw_resource_standby_request
tools.title: Withdraw Resource Standby Request
tools.description: Takes back the standby request the creator has open on the connector, so the picker the bot sent stops waiting for an answer. A creator holds one such request at a time, so there is nothing to name; when none is open the call changes nothing and still succeeds. Only the account holder may do this. Takes no input.

tools.name: list_roles
tools.title: List Roles
tools.description: Lists roles across every team the authenticated user owns or holds a membership in. Each role carries a flat list of `permissions` codes — the same strings the ApiAbility catalog uses as token abilities. Read this when reasoning about authorization or before issuing a new token; cross-reference codes with `subscriby://enums/ability` for human labels.

tools.name: list_subscribers
tools.title: List Subscribers
tools.description: Lists project members (subscribers) with optional filters: `project_id`, `status` (`lead`, `trialing`, `customer`, `churned`, `banned`), `access` (`waiting`: members whose live purchase includes a place waiting for an account they have not connected, the ones `remind_member_to_connect` nudges), and `search` (case-insensitive partial match across name, email and billing email). Paginates with `limit` (1..100) and `page`. Returns both `email` (member-chosen, verified, their portal sign-in credential) and `billing_email` (whatever they gave a payment provider, never verified — identification only, not a contact channel). PII WARNING: both are returned verbatim — scrub before forwarding to any third-party LLM, log sink, or analytics surface.

project_id.description: Optional project UUID to narrow the result.

status.description: Member status filter. One of: lead, trialing, customer, churned, banned

access.description: `waiting` keeps the members whose live purchase includes a place waiting for an account they have not connected; omit for everyone.

search.description: Case-insensitive partial match against name + email.

limit.description: Maximum members to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_subscription_grants
tools.title: List Subscription Grants
tools.description: Lists the access grants a subscription holds: one row per resource (and per pass window) with the connector that gave access, the mode (`bearer_link` invite link, `membership`, `role`, `creator_task`), the state (`pending_identity`, `pending`, `held`, `granted`, `revoked`, `failed`), the connector's reference (the invite link, on a connector that grants by link) and, for a failure, `failure_kind` and `failure_detail`. Answers "does this member actually have access?" — read it instead of inferring access from the payment status. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

subscription_id.description: UUID of the subscription whose grants to list.

tools.name: list_support_conversations
tools.title: List Support Conversations
tools.description: Lists member support conversations, newest activity first. Filters: `project_id`, `status` (`open`, `pending`, `snoozed`, `resolved`), `assigned_to` (user UUID), and `unread_only`. Paginates with `limit` (1..100) and `page`. Each row carries the member name and the last message time so a triage pass needs no follow-up calls. PII WARNING: member names are returned verbatim — scrub before forwarding anywhere outside this conversation. Use get_support_conversation for the message history.

project_id.description: Optional project UUID to narrow the result.

status.description: Conversation status filter. One of: open, pending, snoozed, resolved

assigned_to.description: Only conversations assigned to this team-member user UUID.

unread_only.description: Only conversations with messages the creator has not opened.

limit.description: Maximum conversations to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_team_members
tools.title: List Team Members
tools.description: Lists the collaborators on one team. The owner is prepended as a pseudo-row with `is_owner=true` and `role_id=null`; pivot members follow with their assigned `role_id`. Emails are returned verbatim — these are internal collaborators, not subscribers, so PII handling rules are looser, but still scrub before forwarding to third-party systems.

team_id.description: UUID of the team whose members to list.

tools.name: list_teams
tools.title: List Teams
tools.description: Lists every team the authenticated user owns or holds a membership in. Each row carries `personal` so the personal team is identifiable. Useful before minting a token scoped to a specific team via the dashboard. Team CRUD stays dashboard-only — no `create_team` / `delete_team` tools exist.

tools.name: list_tokens
tools.title: List Personal Access Tokens
tools.description: Lists the authenticated user's own personal access tokens. The plaintext token value is NEVER surfaced — only `id`, `name`, `abilities` (gate codes), `scopes` (`team_id` and `project_ids` extracted from the `scope:team:` / `scope:project:` ability prefixes), `last_used_at`, `expires_at`, and `created_at`. Token ownership IS the permission — no extra ability is required to call. Pair with `revoke_token` to retire a token.

tools.name: list_transactions
tools.title: List Transactions (Keyset)
tools.description: Keyset-paginated transaction listing for one project, ordered reverse-chronologically. Filter by `period` preset or explicit `from`/`to` ISO dates, plus allow-lists for `statuses`, `provider_ids`, `plan_ids`, and `currency_ids`. Pass `cursor` from the previous response's `meta.next_cursor` to continue. Each row carries its owning `project_id`/`project_name`, `plan_id`/`plan_name` and `subscriber_id`/`subscriber_name`, so a payment can be attributed without a follow-up lookup. Raw webhook payloads are never returned. Use this over `list_recent_payments` when walking a long history; reach for `get_earnings_report` when you only need totals.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose transactions to list.

period.description: Period preset — 7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 90d, mtd, qtd, ytd, 1y, all. Defaults to 30d.

from.description: Explicit start date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Overrides period when paired with "to".

to.description: Explicit end date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Overrides period when paired with "from".

statuses.description: Optional payment-status allow-list. Values: successful, failed, pending, refunded.

plan_ids.description: Optional plan-UUID allow-list applied to the parent subscription.

cursor.description: Opaque keyset cursor returned in a prior meta.next_cursor. Pass to continue pagination.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return (1..200, default 50).

tools.name: list_webhook_endpoints
tools.title: List Webhook Endpoints
tools.description: Lists outbound webhook endpoints registered for the token's team. Optionally scoped by `project_id`, or trimmed by `active_only` to hide endpoints with `is_active=false` or `disabled_at` set. Webhook signing secrets are NEVER returned; only `url`, the `events` allow-list, `failure_count`, `consecutive_failures`, and `last_success_at` / `last_failure_at` timestamps. Cross-reference allowed `events` against `subscriby://enums/webhook-event` to confirm coverage.

project_id.description: Optional project UUID. Omit to list team-wide endpoints and all project-scoped endpoints within the team.

active_only.description: When true, hides endpoints with is_active=false or disabled_at set.

tools.name: preview_access_code_cost
tools.title: Preview Access-Code Generation Cost
tools.description: Previews the cost of generating access codes for a plan WITHOUT queuing the batch. Returns `free_remaining`, `chargeable_quantity`, and `cost` (in the creator-tier currency) plus `will_bill_overage` so the agent can surface the charge to a human before any money moves. Always call this before `bulk_generate_access_codes` when `quantity` might exceed the creator-tier free allotment — generation is free, but redemption of overage codes triggers Stripe metered billing.

plan_id.description: UUID of the plan the batch would be attached to.

quantity.description: How many access codes the agent is considering generating (1-10000).

tools.name: preview_broadcast_audience
tools.title: Preview Broadcast Audience
tools.description: Sizes a broadcast without sending anything. Returns every audience segment this project can address with its current recipient count and the estimated send duration. Call this BEFORE `broadcast_message` and show the human the count — a segment that silently resolves to every member is the one mistake a broadcast cannot be taken back from. Omit `audience` to list all segments.

project_id.description: UUID of the project to size a broadcast for.

audience.description: Size one segment only. Omit to receive every segment with its count.

pass_window_id.description: Needed to size the single-window pass segments; without it they report a null count.

plan_id.description: Optional plan UUID. Sizes each segment as narrowed to that plan. Segments that cannot use a plan filter (`lead`, the pass segments) report their unnarrowed count and a null plan_id.

expiring_within_days.description: How far ahead `expiring_soon` looks, 1-90, default 7. Ignored by every other segment.

tools.name: publish_plan
tools.title: Publish or Unpublish Plan
tools.description: Flips a plan's `active` flag. Pass `active=true` to publish (the plan starts accepting checkouts), `active=false` to unpublish (existing subscriptions keep running, but no new checkouts can start). Defaults to `true`. Idempotent — re-calling on a plan already in the target state is a no-op. Emits `plan.activated` or `plan.deactivated`. Plans priced at `0` can only be sold on the Starter and Growth tiers, so publishing one on the Free tier is refused with `TEAM_TIER_REQUIRED` and the plan must be given a price first. Unpublishing is always allowed.

plan_id.description: UUID of the plan to flip.

active.description: Target state — true publishes, false unpublishes. Defaults to true.

tools.name: reorder_plans
tools.title: Reorder Plans
tools.description: Pins the order a project's plans appear in on the public portal and in the project's bot. Pass `plan_ids` in the order buyers should see them; plans left out keep the built-in order (passes, then seasons, then subscriptions, cheapest first) after the pinned ones. Pass an empty list to clear every pin and return to the built-in order. Only active plans are shown to buyers, but inactive ones may be pinned so they take their place when published. Idempotent. Emits `plan.order_changed`. An id from another project is refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose storefront is arranged.

plan_ids.description: Plan UUIDs in the order buyers should see them. Empty clears every pin and restores the built-in order.

tools.name: reply_support_conversation
tools.title: Reply to Support Conversation
tools.description: Sends a reply to a member in a support conversation. THIS MESSAGE REACHES A REAL PERSON on their connector — confirm the wording with the creator before calling, and never invent facts about their subscription, refunds or access. Requires `conversation_id` and `body` (max 4000 characters). Set `internal` to true to record a private note for the creator instead, which is never delivered to the member. The reply is prefixed with the project support name so the member sees a human, not the bot. Delivery is queued: a success here means recorded and queued, not yet received.

conversation_id.description: UUID of the support conversation to reply in.

body.description: The reply text, max 4000 characters. Reaches the member verbatim.

internal.description: Record a creator-only note instead of sending to the member.

reply_to_message_id.description: Optional. UUID of a message in this same conversation to quote above the reply, the way a chat client shows a threaded reply.

tools.name: resolve_support_conversation
tools.title: Resolve Support Conversation
tools.description: Marks a support conversation resolved, clearing it from the open queue and emitting support.conversation.resolved. Requires `conversation_id`. Not destructive: the thread and its history are kept, and it reopens by itself the moment the member writes again. Resolve only what has actually been answered — a resolved thread stops showing in the creator triage list.

conversation_id.description: UUID of the support conversation to resolve.

tools.name: revoke_token
tools.title: Revoke Personal Access Token
tools.description: Revokes one of the authenticated user's own personal access tokens by id. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `token_id` with a human before calling — any external integration using the revoked token will start failing immediately on the next request. Refuses self-revocation; the token authenticating this call cannot delete its own row (returns `VALIDATION_FAILED`). Token ownership IS the permission — foreign token ids return `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` to prevent existence leaks. Idempotent — re-calling on an already-revoked id returns `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

token_id.description: UUID of the token to revoke. Must belong to the authenticated user. Cannot be the id of the token authenticating this call.

tools.name: unban_member
tools.title: Unban Member
tools.description: Lifts a ban on a project member — status rolls to `Churned`, and downstream payment pipelines promote the member back to `Customer` on the next successful payment. Idempotent — re-calling on an already-unbanned member is a no-op. Emits `member.unbanned`. Use after `ban_member` to reverse a ban that was applied by mistake or expired.

member_id.description: UUID of the banned project member to unban.

tools.name: unlink_member_identity
tools.title: Unlink Member Identity
tools.description: Disconnects one of a project member's connector accounts: it no longer signs them in to the portal and the project's bot no longer knows them by it. Refused when it is the member's last way to sign in (no verified email, linked Google account or other connected account remains). Pass the link `id` from `list_member_identities`, not the account's external id. Emits `member.identity_unlinked`. Not idempotent: a second call answers `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

tools.name: unlink_resource
tools.title: Unlink Resource
tools.description: Clears the connector place (`space`) from a resource, reverting it to an unlinked placeholder the creator can relink later through the connector with `request_resource_link`. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `resource_id` with a human before calling — every plan that links this resource stops granting access through the connector on the next sync. Idempotent — re-calling on an already-unlinked resource is a no-op. Emits `project.resource.unlinked`.

resource_id.description: UUID of the resource to unlink.

tools.name: update_project
tools.title: Update Project
tools.description: Applies a partial update to an existing project — only fields you pass are touched, omitted fields keep their current value. Updating `handle` moves the portal URL (see `get_portal_url`); every address the project answered on before keeps redirecting to the current one, and a blank handle switches the portal page off. Idempotent — re-calling with the same payload converges to the same state. Emits `project.updated` with a `changes` map.

project_id.description: UUID of the project to update.

description.description: New description. Max 1000 chars, HTML is filtered.

handle.description: New URL-friendly handle, on every tier. Alpha-dash lowercase, 5-255 chars, unique across every project's current and former handles; the old address keeps redirecting.

terms.description: URL to the terms page. Max 255 chars.

privacy.description: URL to the privacy page. Max 255 chars.

storefront_arrangement.description: How the portal, the embed and the bot order the plans on offer: "manual" is the order pinned through `reorder_plans` with passes, seasons and then subscriptions behind it; "live" puts the passes and seasons whose access is on now first, the one ending soonest at the top, then those opening soonest, then the pinned order. "live" needs the project owner's time-limited passes capability (Growth, or the Passes Addon) and is refused with `TEAM_TIER_REQUIRED` without it; "manual" is always accepted.

active.description: Flip to false to archive, true to restore.

outage_compensations.description: Whether members whose paid access overlapped a connector outage of an hour or more have it extended by the outage length when the connector answers again. Defaults to true on every project.

hide_branding.description: Take the "Powered by Subscriby" mark off the portal page, its social card and the bot (true) or put it back (false). Off by default on every plan; true needs a Starter or Growth tier (TEAM_TIER_REQUIRED otherwise), and a project whose owner lost the tier keeps the switch and shows the mark until the plan returns.

tools.name: update_portal_design
tools.title: Update Portal Design
tools.description: Changes some keys of a project's portal design in its draft; anything you omit keeps its drafted value and members keep seeing the published design until `publish_portal_design`. Requires `project_id`; every other argument is one key of the document `get_portal_design` returns, in the same shape: a `preset` recolours the six colours unless a colour is sent beside it, a text colour that blends into the surface or the background is refused, `featured_plan_id` must be one of the project's plans, `locales` must carry `default_locale`, and every list has its ceiling. Pictures are stored over REST (`POST /v1/projects/{project}/portal-design/images/{slot}`) and their addresses written here. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` naming the key. Unknown or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose portal design to change.

preset.description: The palette the colours started from: `classic`, `dark`, `midnight`, `paper`, `pastel` or `bold`. Sending it recolours the six colours below from the preset and keeps the colour mode and the grid; send a colour beside it to override that one.

color_mode.description: `light` or `dark` paints one palette for everyone; `system` paints the light one and switches to the preset's drawn dark palette when the visitor's browser asks for a dark scheme.

accent.description: The accent, on the buttons, the highlights and the chosen plan's ring, as a six-digit lowercase hex such as `#a3e635`. The text drawn on it is picked by luminance.

accent_secondary.description: The second accent, on the pass-series and pass strips, as a hex colour; `null` paints the preset's own.

background.description: The page colour behind the cards, as a hex colour.

grid.description: Whether the faint dotted grid is drawn over the page colour.

surface.description: The cards' colour, as a hex colour.

text.description: The body text colour, as a hex colour. It must read on the surface and on the background: a pair under a 3:1 contrast ratio is refused.

heading.description: The colour of the project's name and every heading, as a hex colour, under the same contrast rule as `text`.

muted.description: The colour of the captions, the labels and the small print, as a hex colour, under the same contrast rule as `text`.

tagline.description: One line under the project's name, up to 80 characters, or `null` for none.

social_links.description: Up to 12 links under the card, each `{network, url, label}`: `network` one of `website`, `instagram`, `x`, `youtube`, `tiktok`, `facebook`, `linkedin`, `discord`, `telegram`, `whatsapp`, `threads`, `custom`; `url` an https address; `label` the name shown for a `custom` link, up to 40 characters, ignored on the others.

font_display.description: The face of the headings: `asap-condensed`, `inter`, `poppins`, `montserrat`, `space-grotesk`, `bebas-neue`, `oswald`, `dm-serif-display`, `playfair-display`, `lora`, `manrope` or `sora`.

font_body.description: The face of everything but the headings, from the same twelve as `font_display`.

type_scale.description: `compact`, `regular` or `large`: one multiplier on every text size.

radius.description: `sharp`, `soft` or `round` corners on the cards and the fields.

button_fill.description: `accent` fills the buttons with the accent, `dark` with the heading colour, `outline` draws them hollow.

card_border.description: Whether the cards carry a hairline border.

arrangement.description: `sidebar_left` or `sidebar_right` put the card beside the plans, `stacked` puts it above them, `hero` runs the banner across the top.

content_width.description: `narrow`, `regular` or `wide`: how wide the page runs.

sticky_sidebar.description: Whether the sidebar card stays in view while the plans scroll.

plan_grid.description: `list`, `two` or `three`: how many plan cards sit side by side.

plans_heading.description: Whether the heading over the plans is shown.

metrics_subscribers.description: Whether the member count is shown on the card.

metrics_followers.description: Whether the follower count is shown on the card.

metrics_threshold.description: The count a figure must reach before it is shown, 0 to 1,000,000, so a young project never shows a small number.

plans_title.description: The heading over the plans, up to 60 characters; `null` for the built-in wording.

plans_subtitle.description: The line under that heading, up to 120 characters; `null` for the built-in wording.

label_login.description: The Login button's label, up to 24 characters; `null` for the built-in wording.

label_share.description: The Share button's label, up to 24 characters; `null` for the built-in wording.

label_subscribe.description: The button on every plan card, up to 24 characters; `null` for the built-in wording.

checkout_title.description: The checkout's heading, up to 60 characters; `null` for the built-in wording.

checkout_subtitle.description: The line under the checkout's heading, up to 120 characters; `null` for the built-in wording.

checkout_note.description: A note under the checkout, up to 240 characters; `null` for none.

success_title.description: The heading of the thank-you screen, up to 60 characters; `null` for the built-in wording.

success_message.description: The thank-you screen's message, up to 400 characters; `null` for the built-in wording.

perks_title.description: The heading over the perks, up to 60 characters; `null` for the built-in one.

perks.description: Up to 12 perks, each a line of up to 120 characters; the block shows only with at least one.

faq_title.description: The heading over the questions, up to 60 characters; `null` for the built-in one.

faq.description: Up to 12 questions, each `{question, answer}`, the question up to 160 characters and the answer up to 800, both required.

about_name.description: The name on the card about the creator, up to 60 characters, or `null`; the card shows when a name or a bio is set.

about_bio.description: The bio on the card about the creator, up to 600 characters, or `null`.

custom_button_label.description: The second button's label, up to 24 characters, sent together with `custom_button_url` or both `null`.

custom_button_url.description: Where the second button leads, an https or http address up to 255 characters, sent together with `custom_button_label` or both `null`.

footer_refund_url.description: The refund policy link in the footer, an https or http address, or `null`.

footer_contact_url.description: The contact link in the footer, an https, http or `mailto:` address, or `null`.

footer_imprint_url.description: The imprint link in the footer, an https or http address, or `null`.

footer_line.description: A line of small print in the footer, up to 120 characters, or `null`.

footer_help.description: Whether the Help link is shown in the footer.

announcement_text.description: The strip across the top of the page, up to 160 characters, or `null` for no strip.

announcement_url.description: Where the strip leads, an https or http address, or `null`.

announcement_starts_at.description: When the strip starts showing, ISO 8601 in any zone and stored in UTC, or `null` for at once.

announcement_ends_at.description: When the strip comes down, ISO 8601 and after the start, or `null` for never.

video_url.description: A YouTube or Vimeo address in any shape the share button gives, stored as the canonical watch address, or `null` for no video.

gallery_title.description: The heading over the gallery, up to 60 characters; `null` for the built-in one.

gallery.description: Up to 8 picture addresses, each stored through `POST /v1/projects/{project}/portal-design/images/gallery`.

testimonials_title.description: The heading over the quotes, up to 60 characters; `null` for the built-in one.

testimonials.description: Up to 12 quotes from members, each `{quote, name, subtitle, avatar_url}`: the words up to 300 characters and the name up to 60, both required; `subtitle` what they are, up to 60 characters, or `null`; `avatar_url` a photo stored through `POST /v1/projects/{project}/portal-design/images/avatar`, or `null` for the first letter of the name.

sidebar_items.description: The sidebar card's parts in order, each `{key, shown}` with `key` one of `tagline`, `metrics`, `buttons`, `description`, `social_links`, `footer`, every key exactly once; a part left out is appended, shown.

content_blocks.description: The blocks under the plans in order, each `{key, shown}` with `key` one of `perks`, `about`, `faq`, `video`, `gallery`, `testimonials`, every key exactly once; a block left out is appended, shown.

locale_switcher.description: Whether the list of languages under the card is shown.

featured_plan_id.description: The plan that carries the Most popular badge, one of the project's own plan ids, or `null` for none.

coupon_box.description: `always` shows the coupon box on every checkout; `link` shows it only once a coupon arrived with the visit.

share_button.description: Whether the Share button is shown in the header.

share_networks.description: Which networks the share sheet offers, kept in the sheet's own order: `bluesky`, `buffer`, `email`, `facebook`, `flipboard`, `line`, `linkedin`, `mix`, `pinterest`, `reddit`, `telegram`, `threads`, `tumblr`, `x`, `vk`, `whatsapp`, `xing`.

login_button.description: Whether the Login button is shown in the header.

social_proof.description: Whether a line over the plans says how many members joined in the last seven days; it shows only from three up.

seats_badges.description: Whether a pass series card shows how many seats are left.

seo_indexable.description: Whether search engines may list the portal; `false` adds a noindex directive. A portal the project's own readiness keeps out stays unlisted either way.

seo_social_card.description: Whether a shared link unfurls with a card image; `false` leaves the title and the description alone.

pixel_meta.description: The creator's own Meta Pixel id, 10 to 20 digits, or `null`.

pixel_ga4.description: The creator's own Google Analytics 4 measurement id, `G-` followed by 4 to 15 letters or digits, or `null`.

pixel_tiktok.description: The creator's own TikTok Pixel id, 10 to 30 letters or digits, or `null`.

pixel_google_ads.description: The creator's own Google Ads conversion id, `AW-` followed by 6 to 12 digits, or `null`.

custom_css.description: A stylesheet of up to 16,384 characters printed after the theme so its rules win; refused when it would load, run or escape (`@import`, `url(`, `expression(`, `javascript:`, a closing `style` tag and the like); `null` for none.

seo_title_suffix.description: The words after the project's name in the page title, up to 60 characters, or `null` for the built-in ones.

seo_description.description: The description search engines and shared links show, up to 160 characters, or `null` for one cut from the project's text.

social_card_url.description: A card image of the creator's own, stored through `POST /v1/projects/{project}/portal-design/images/card` and sent in the generated card's place, or `null` for the generated card.

default_locale.description: The language the portal's own address opens in, as a code from `locales`, or `null` for the platform's default.

locales.description: The languages the switcher offers, as codes from `en`, `fr`, `es`, `it`, `hi`, `bn`, `de`, `pt`, `tr`, `si`, never empty and always carrying `default_locale`.

tools.name: publish_portal_design
tools.title: Publish Portal Design
tools.description: Makes a project's drafted portal design the one members see; the portal, the embed and the social card paint with it on their next render, and `project.design_published` is emitted naming the sections that changed. Requires `project_id`. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` when nothing is drafted. Unknown or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose drafted portal design to publish.

tools.name: discard_portal_design_draft
tools.title: Discard Portal Design Draft
tools.description: Throws a project's drafted portal design away and keeps what members see; a picture only the draft named is removed with it. Requires `project_id`. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` when nothing is drafted. Unknown or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose portal design draft to discard.

tools.name: update_support_settings
tools.title: Update Support Settings
tools.description: Changes a project's support inbox settings; anything you omit keeps its stored value. Requires `project_id`. Optional: `enabled`, `relay_mode` (`owner_dm`, `forum_group` or `none`; other values are refused; `forum_group` starts relaying once the project bot has been added to a Topics-enabled group as an administrator), `agent_name` (up to 60 chars, null to clear), `auto_reply` (up to 1000 chars, null to clear), `notify_email`, `copilot_answers` (Subscriby Copilot answers members' own-subscription questions and what the Knowledge covers in the inbox and the project bot, marked as automated) and `copilot_portal` (the same Copilot in a chat on the portal page). Emits `support.settings.updated` with the changed fields. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` per field. Turning support off stops new member threads reaching the inbox; existing threads are kept. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose support settings to change.

enabled.description: Whether members can open support threads with the bot.

relay_mode.description: Where new threads go besides the dashboard inbox: "owner_dm" forwards them to the creator on their connector, "forum_group" opens each thread as a topic in the group the project bot administers, "none" keeps them in the inbox only.

agent_name.description: The name members see on replies, up to 60 characters. Pass null to use the project name.

auto_reply.description: The message sent automatically when a member opens a thread, up to 1000 characters. Pass null for none.

notify_email.description: Whether the creator is emailed about new threads.

copilot_answers.description: Whether Subscriby Copilot answers members' own-subscription questions and what the project's Knowledge covers in the inbox and the project bot, marked as automated.

copilot_portal.description: Whether a signed-in member finds the Copilot in a chat on the portal page.

tools.name: update_resource
tools.title: Update Resource
tools.description: Retitles, describes or switches a project resource; anything you omit keeps its stored value. Requires `resource_id`. Optional: `title` (5..255 chars), `description` (up to 1000 chars of well-formed HTML, or null to clear) and `active`. The resource `type` and its connector place (`chat_id`) are fixed and silently ignored here — a place is linked through the connector with `request_resource_link` and unlinked with `unlink_resource`. Emits `project.resource.updated` with the changed fields. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

resource_id.description: UUID of the resource to change.

description.description: New description, up to 1000 characters of well-formed HTML. Pass null or an empty string to clear it.

active.description: true offers the resource on the plans that link it, false switches it off without touching those plans.

tools.name: update_plan
tools.title: Update Plan
tools.description: Changes one or more fields of an existing plan; anything you omit keeps its stored value. Requires `plan_id`. Optional: `name`, `description`, `price`, `currency_id`, `active`, `eligibility`, `resources` (the full list of resource UUIDs the plan grants — it REPLACES the current list), and the ONE nested block the plan's `kind` names: `billing` for a subscription, `pass` for a pass, `pass_series` for a season (same fields as `create_plan`; a block of another kind is refused). `kind` itself cannot change — create a new plan instead. Emits `plan.updated`; to flip `active` alone with its own `plan.activated` / `plan.deactivated` event, call `publish_plan`. Refused with `TEAM_TIER_REQUIRED` when the change needs a tier the project owner lacks (a free price, time-limited passes), with `VALIDATION_FAILED` per field otherwise. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

plan_id.description: UUID of the plan to change.

name.description: Plan name (min 5, max 255 chars, unique per project).

description.description: Plan description. Max 1000 chars, HTML is filtered. Pass an empty string to clear.

price.description: What one purchase costs, as a decimal. At least the $1.00 USD equivalent unless 0, which makes the plan free and requires the Starter or Growth tier.

currency_id.description: UUID of the currency. Must be supported by an active payment method on the project.

active.description: true publishes the plan, false takes it off sale; existing subscriptions keep running either way.

sales_cap.description: Pause the plan automatically after this many successful purchases (1-100000). Changing it restarts the count; null removes the limit.

eligibility.description: Audience restrictions: {newcomers_only?: bool, customers_only?: bool, churned_only?: bool, single_use?: bool, access_codes_only?: bool}. The first three are mutually exclusive.

resources.description: The full list of project_resources UUIDs this plan grants access to; replaces the current list. Must not be empty on kind subscription or kind pass.

billing.description: Only on a plan of kind subscription. {billing_cycle: days|weeks|months|years|lifetime, billing_cycle_count: int 1-99, recurring?: bool, disabled_renewal?: bool, trial_days?: int 0-365, trial_cardless?: bool, trial_type?: string}. lifetime requires billing_cycle_count=1.

pass.description: Only on a plan of kind pass. {timezone: IANA zone, schedule_mode?: repeating|fixed, recurrence?: daily|weekly|monthly, recurrence_ends_at?: ISO-8601, sales_cutoff_minutes?: int, sales_cutoff_anchor?: before_start|before_end, slots?: array, windows?: array}; the same shape `create_plan` documents.

pass_series.description: Only on a plan of kind pass_series. {window_ids?: array of pass-window UUIDs, prevent_overlaps?: bool, sales_cutoff_minutes?: int, sales_cutoff_anchor?: string, seat_cap?: int, successor_plan_id?: UUID, presale_hours?: int, blackout_window_ids?: array, rules?: array}; the same shape `create_plan` documents. Window ids come from `list_pass_windows`.

tools.name: update_coupon
tools.title: Update Coupon
tools.description: Changes one or more fields of an existing coupon code; anything you omit keeps its stored value. Requires `coupon_id`. Optional: `code` (letters, numbers and dashes, 3..64, stored uppercase, must be unused in the project), `name`, `discount_type` (`percentage` or `fixed`), `discount_value` (1..100 for a percentage, any amount above zero for a fixed discount), `currency_id` (needed when the effective type is fixed and the code has none yet; cleared automatically for a percentage), `max_redemptions` (null for unlimited), `max_redemptions_per_user`, `minimum_amount` (null for none), `starts_at` / `expires_at` (ISO 8601, null to clear; the end must fall after the start), `active`, and `plan_ids` (an empty list covers every plan in the project, including ones added later). The discount still applies to the FIRST payment only. Emits `coupon.updated`. Refused with `TEAM_TIER_REQUIRED` when the project owner's tier no longer includes coupons, with `VALIDATION_FAILED` per field otherwise.

coupon_id.description: UUID of the coupon to change.

code.description: New code subscribers type at checkout. Letters, numbers and dashes only, 3 to 64 characters. Stored uppercase; must not already exist in the project.

discount_type.description: Either "percentage" or "fixed". Switching to fixed needs a currency_id unless the code already has one.

discount_value.description: For percentage, 1..100. For fixed, an amount greater than zero in the coupon's currency.

currency_id.description: Currency UUID for a fixed discount. Ignored and cleared for a percentage.

max_redemptions.description: Total uses allowed across everyone. Pass null for unlimited.

max_redemptions_per_user.description: How many times one subscriber may use the code.

minimum_amount.description: Only apply the code when the plan costs at least this much. Pass null for no minimum.

starts_at.description: ISO 8601 instant the code becomes usable. Pass null to start immediately.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 instant the code stops working. Pass null for no end date. Must fall after the start.

plan_ids.description: Plan UUIDs to restrict the code to. An empty list covers every plan in the project, including ones added later.

tools.name: update_canned_reply
tools.title: Update Canned Reply
tools.description: Changes one or more fields of a saved support reply; anything you omit keeps its stored value. Requires `project_id` and `canned_reply_id`. Optional: `title` (2..80 chars), `body` (2..4000 chars), `shortcut` (letters, numbers, dashes and underscores, up to 30, unique within the project; null clears it) and `sort_order` (0..999). Emits `support.canned_reply.updated` with the changed fields. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` per field. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the snippet belongs to.

canned_reply_id.description: UUID of the saved reply to change.

shortcut.description: New slash-command, unique within the project. Pass null to clear it.

sort_order.description: New position in the picker, 0 to 999.

tools.name: unblock_support_contact
tools.title: Unblock Support Contact
tools.description: Lets the member behind a support thread write in again after `block_support_contact`. Requires `conversation_id`. Messages dropped while blocked are gone; only new ones arrive. Emits `support.conversation.unblocked` when the block is lifted. Idempotent — a member who is not blocked is a no-op and emits nothing. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

conversation_id.description: UUID of the support conversation whose member to unblock.

tools.name: test_webhook_endpoint
tools.title: Test Webhook Endpoint
tools.description: Queues a synthetic test event to an endpoint so its consumer can be checked end to end. Requires `endpoint_id`. Returns the queued delivery in the `get_webhook_delivery` row shape; poll that tool for the target's `response_status` once the worker has posted it. Only the creator who registered the endpoint or the team owner may fire a test; a fellow team member is refused with `FORBIDDEN`. Unknown or foreign ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

endpoint_id.description: UUID of the webhook endpoint to send a test event to.

tools.name: sync_payment_method_plans
tools.title: Sync Payment Method Plans
tools.description: Queues a push of the project owner's plans into a payment method's gateway catalogue (Stripe products and prices, Polar products, Kelviq plans, PayPal, Razorpay or CoinPayments plans). Requires `project_id` and `payment_method_id`. Answers with status "sync_queued": the work runs in the background and each plan reports through the plan-sync webhook events as it lands. A gateway that keeps no catalogue (connector currencies, access codes, the redirect gateways) is refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Idempotent — queuing twice pushes the same catalogue twice. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the method belongs to.

payment_method_id.description: UUID of the payment method whose gateway catalogue to refresh.

tools.name: start_next_season
tools.title: Start Next Season
tools.description: Duplicates a finished pass series into its next season: a NEW inactive pass_series plan with the same price, settings, resources and rules but an empty slate, linked from the old season as its successor so the presale reaches every current holder. Requires `plan_id` of a plan whose kind is `pass_series`; any other kind is refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Emits `plan.created`. Not idempotent — every call creates another season, so call it once per season. Then add dates to the new slate with `update_plan` (the `pass_series.window_ids` or `rules`) and put it on sale with `publish_plan`. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

plan_id.description: UUID of the finished pass_series plan to duplicate into its next season.

tools.name: rotate_webhook_endpoint_secret
tools.title: Rotate Webhook Endpoint Secret
tools.description: Replaces an endpoint's signing secret. Requires `endpoint_id`. The new secret is returned in this response only, under `secret`, and can never be read again — hand it to the consumer immediately, because deliveries are signed with it from now on and the previous secret stops verifying. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `endpoint_id` with a human before calling. Only the creator who registered the endpoint or the team owner may rotate it; a fellow team member is refused with `FORBIDDEN`. Not idempotent — every call mints another secret. Unknown or foreign ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

endpoint_id.description: UUID of the webhook endpoint whose secret to replace.

tools.name: retry_webhook_delivery
tools.title: Retry Webhook Delivery
tools.description: Replays one failed or dead-lettered webhook delivery from the start of the retry ladder, posting the same event to the same endpoint again. Requires `delivery_id`. A pending or already-delivered row is refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED`, because replaying it would post the event twice. Returns the delivery row, pending again. Unknown or foreign ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

delivery_id.description: UUID of the failed or dead-lettered delivery to replay.

tools.name: retry_dead_webhook_deliveries
tools.title: Retry Dead Webhook Deliveries
tools.description: Replays every webhook delivery the team dead-lettered recently, once the consumer is fixed. Optional `since` (ISO 8601, not in the future) names the instant the window opens at; omit it for the last 24 hours, the same window the dashboard's Replay button uses. Answers with how many rows were `retried` and the `since` used. Each replayed row posts its event again, so confirm the consumer is healthy first. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` for a malformed or future `since`.

since.description: ISO 8601 instant; rows dead-lettered at or after it are replayed. Defaults to 24 hours ago.

tools.name: resume_webhook_endpoint
tools.title: Resume Webhook Endpoint
tools.description: Starts deliveries to a paused endpoint again and clears its consecutive-failure streak, so a target that was fixed is not disabled again on its first miss. Requires `endpoint_id`. Events raised while it was paused are not replayed; use `retry_dead_webhook_deliveries` for rows that dead-lettered before the pause. Only the creator who registered the endpoint or the team owner may resume it; a fellow team member is refused with `FORBIDDEN`. Idempotent — an already-active endpoint is a no-op. Unknown or foreign ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

endpoint_id.description: UUID of the webhook endpoint to resume.

tools.name: restore_project
tools.title: Restore Project
