tools.description: Restores an archived project — flips `active` back to true so checkout, portal and bot flows accept new subscribers again. Requires `project_id`. The reverse of `archive_project`; it cannot bring back a project removed with `delete_project`, which is permanent. Idempotent — re-calling on a project that is already active is a no-op and emits nothing. Emits `project.restored` to every subscribed webhook endpoint when the flag actually changes. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the archived project to restore.

tools.name: reopen_support_conversation
tools.title: Reopen Support Conversation
tools.description: Puts a resolved support thread back in the open queue so it shows in the creator's triage list again. Requires `conversation_id`. The reverse of `resolve_support_conversation`; a member writing again reopens the thread by itself, so call this only when the creator wants to follow up first. Idempotent — an already-open thread is a no-op. Emits `support.conversation.reopened`. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

conversation_id.description: UUID of the support conversation to reopen.

tools.name: remind_pass_window_queue
tools.title: Remind Pass Window Queue
tools.description: Nudges everyone who bought a window but has not come through their grant yet, re-sending it. Requires `project_id` and `window_id`. Answers with how many holders the connector accepted the message for; a window that has ended or been cancelled reminds nobody and answers 0. THIS MESSAGES REAL PEOPLE: confirm with the creator before calling and do not repeat it within the same window. For one holder, call `remind_pass_holder`. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose pass plans own the window.

window_id.description: UUID of the window whose missing holders to nudge.

tools.name: remind_pass_holder
tools.title: Remind Pass Holder
tools.description: Nudges ONE pass holder who bought a window but has not come through their grant yet, re-sending it. Requires `subscription_id`. Answers `reminded: true` when the connector accepted the message, `reminded: false` when there was nothing to send — the subscription holds no window, the window has ended or been cancelled, the holder has already queued, or they are unreachable on their connector — which is a normal answer, not an error. THIS MESSAGES A REAL PERSON: read the subscription back first and do not repeat the nudge within the same window. To remind everyone still missing from a window at once, call `remind_pass_window_queue`. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

subscription_id.description: UUID of the pass holder's subscription.

tools.name: remind_member_to_connect
tools.title: Remind Member To Connect
tools.description: Reminds ONE member that a place of their purchase still waits for an account they have not connected (a place on one platform bought through the bot of another, say), by mail and in their chat, with the door that connects it. Requires `subscription_id`; find candidates with `list_subscribers` and `access: waiting`. Answers `reminded` true when the message went out and false when nothing was sent: no place waits, the member was reminded within the last day or stopped the follow-ups, or the purchase ended.

subscription_id.description: UUID of the purchase whose place waits for an account.

tools.name: reissue_subscription_grants
tools.title: Reissue Subscription Grants
tools.description: Revokes the access grants a member holds on a subscription — every resource, or only `resource_id` — and has fresh ones issued by the same job that grants at purchase; the bot sends the member the new links. The members page's "Refresh invite links" for agents: use it when a link expired or leaked, or after a chat's admins cleared a ban. Answers `reissued` (grants withdrawn) and `status: reissue_queued`; read the fresh grants back with `list_subscription_grants`. Raises `member.resource_reissued` per grant and `member.resource_added` per fresh one. THIS KILLS LIVE LINKS AND MESSAGES A REAL PERSON: read the subscription back first and never loop it. A subscription that is not active is `VALIDATION_FAILED`; unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids, or a `resource_id` the plan does not grant, surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

subscription_id.description: UUID of the subscription whose grants to reissue.

resource_id.description: UUID of one resource of the plan to reissue alone; omit to reissue every resource the subscription grants.

tools.name: pause_webhook_endpoint
tools.title: Pause Webhook Endpoint
tools.description: Stops deliveries to an endpoint without removing it; events raised while paused are not queued for it. Requires `endpoint_id`. Resume with `resume_webhook_endpoint`; the secret is unchanged. Only the creator who registered the endpoint or the team owner may pause it; a fellow team member is refused with `FORBIDDEN`. Idempotent — an already-paused endpoint is a no-op. Unknown or foreign ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

endpoint_id.description: UUID of the webhook endpoint to pause.

tools.name: list_webhook_deliveries
tools.title: List Webhook Deliveries
tools.description: Lists the team's outbound webhook deliveries newest first, with each row's event, status, attempt count, the target's response status and excerpt, the payload that was posted and when it was delivered or dead-lettered. Optional `status` tab: `all` (default), `pending`, `delivered`, `failed` or `dead`; any other value is `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page`. Use it to see why a consumer rejected an event before calling `retry_webhook_delivery` or `retry_dead_webhook_deliveries`.

status.description: Tab of the delivery log: all, pending, delivered, failed or dead. Defaults to all.

limit.description: Maximum deliveries to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_canned_replies
tools.title: List Canned Replies
tools.description: Lists a project's saved support replies in the order the creator arranged them. Requires `project_id`. Each row carries the `shortcut` a creator types in the thread composer to pull the snippet in and its `sort_order`. Use before `reply_support_conversation` to answer with the creator's own wording. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope project ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose saved replies to list.

tools.name: get_webhook_endpoint
tools.title: Get Webhook Endpoint
tools.description: Fetches one of the team's outbound webhook endpoints by UUID. Requires `endpoint_id`. Same row shape as `list_webhook_endpoints`; the signing secret is NEVER returned. Unknown or foreign ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

endpoint_id.description: UUID of the webhook endpoint to fetch.

tools.name: get_webhook_delivery
tools.title: Get Webhook Delivery
tools.description: Fetches one outbound webhook delivery by UUID: its event, status, attempts, the target's response status and excerpt, the payload that was posted and its timestamps. Requires `delivery_id`. Same row shape as `list_webhook_deliveries`. Unknown or foreign ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

delivery_id.description: UUID of the webhook delivery to fetch.

tools.name: get_support_settings
tools.title: Get Support Settings
tools.description: Reads a project's support inbox settings: whether member support is `enabled`, the `relay_mode` (`owner_dm` forwards each thread to the creator on their connector, `forum_group` opens each thread as a topic in the linked group, `none` keeps it in the dashboard inbox only), the `agent_name` shown to members, the `auto_reply` sent on a new thread, whether `notify_email` is on, and the two Copilot switches: `copilot_answers` (the Copilot answers members in the inbox and the project bot) and `copilot_portal` (and in a chat on the portal page). Requires `project_id`. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose support settings to read.

tools.name: get_subscription
tools.title: Get Subscription
tools.description: Fetches one subscription by UUID: its plan, subscriber, payment method, payment status, price, trial end, end date, whether it was cancelled, when an access code was redeemed, and its access `grants` (one per resource and pass window, with connector, mode, state and failure). The same fields the REST subscription payload carries. Use before `cancel_subscription`, `pause_subscription` or `remind_pass_holder` to read the current state back rather than assuming it. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

subscription_id.description: UUID of the subscription to fetch.

tools.name: get_subscriber
tools.title: Get Subscriber
tools.description: Fetches one project member (subscriber) by UUID. Same row shape as `list_subscribers`, including both `email` (member-chosen, verified) and `billing_email` (whatever they gave a payment provider). PII WARNING: both are returned verbatim — scrub before forwarding to any third-party LLM, log sink, or analytics surface. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

member_id.description: UUID of the project member to fetch.

tools.name: get_plan
tools.title: Get Plan
tools.description: Fetches one subscription plan by UUID. Same row shape as `list_plans`: the row carries a `kind` — subscription, pass or pass_series — and that kind names the ONE nested block accompanying it (`billing`, `pass` or `pass_series`), plus `cadence`, the human-readable duration string the portal and bot show. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

plan_id.description: UUID of the plan to fetch.

tools.name: get_payment_method
tools.title: Get Payment Method
tools.description: Fetches one configured payment method of a project by UUID. Requires `project_id` and `payment_method_id`. Same row shape as `list_payment_methods`: only `id`, `provider`, `connector`, `mode`, `active` and `created_at` — provider secrets, webhook signing secrets and Stripe Connect account ids are never surfaced. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the method belongs to.

payment_method_id.description: UUID of the payment method to fetch.

tools.name: get_pass_window
tools.title: Get Pass Window
tools.description: Fetches one dated access window of a project's pass plans by UUID. Requires `project_id` and `window_id`. Same row shape as `list_pass_windows`: the instant it opens and closes, its local range in the plan's timezone, its lifecycle `status`, whether it is `sellable` right now and how many `holders` bought it. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose pass plans own the window.

window_id.description: UUID of the window to fetch.

tools.name: get_coupon
tools.title: Get Coupon
tools.description: Fetches one coupon code by UUID, with its discount, limits, redemption tally, plan restriction and whether it is redeemable right now. Same row shape as `list_coupons`. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

coupon_id.description: UUID of the coupon to fetch.

tools.name: get_broadcast
tools.title: Get Broadcast
tools.description: Fetches one broadcast by its `broadcast_id` (the id `broadcast_message` answered with): who sent it and from where, the audience, the tallies, `progress.line` as the creator reads it, the failures by kind, and under `failures` the first fifty members it could not reach with the connector's reason for each. Same row shape as `list_broadcasts`. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

broadcast_id.description: UUID of the broadcast to fetch.

tools.name: get_canned_reply
tools.title: Get Canned Reply
tools.description: Fetches one saved support reply by UUID. Requires `project_id` and `canned_reply_id`. Same row shape as `list_canned_replies`. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the snippet belongs to.

canned_reply_id.description: UUID of the saved reply to fetch.

tools.name: disconnect_connector
tools.title: Disconnect Connector
tools.description: Disconnects a project's installation of one connector: the connector withdraws it on its platform, the credentials are wiped and the installation turns `disconnected`; members keep the access they hold, grants, resources, plans and identities are untouched, and the creator can connect it again from the dashboard. Raises `connector.disconnected`. An installation already disconnected is left alone. `CONNECTOR_NOT_INSTALLED` when the project has no installation of the connector.

project_id.description: UUID of the project.

connector.description: The connector key, as `list_connectors` returns it.

tools.name: delete_webhook_endpoint
tools.title: Delete Webhook Endpoint
tools.description: Removes an outbound webhook endpoint; deliveries to it stop at once and its delivery log is kept. Requires `endpoint_id`. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `endpoint_id` with a human before calling — an integration listening on it goes dark. Only the creator who registered the endpoint or the team owner may remove it; a fellow team member is refused with `FORBIDDEN`. Idempotent — an already-deleted id surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, exactly as an unknown or foreign id does.

endpoint_id.description: UUID of the webhook endpoint to remove.

tools.name: delete_project
tools.title: Delete Project
tools.description: Permanently deletes a project by UUID. There is no soft-delete and no undo: the row is removed, and its plans, subscribers, subscriptions, resources, coupons, payment methods and support threads go with it through database cascades. Requires `project_id`. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `project_id` with a human before calling. To stop sales while keeping the history, call `archive_project` instead. Emits `project.deleted` BEFORE the row disappears so webhook listeners receive the final snapshot. Idempotent — re-calling on an already-deleted id returns `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, exactly as an unknown or out-of-scope id does.

project_id.description: UUID of the project to delete permanently.

tools.name: delete_plan
tools.title: Delete Plan
tools.description: Soft-deletes a plan so it disappears from the portal, the bot and every list; existing subscriptions keep their history and keep running to their end. Requires `plan_id`. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `plan_id` with a human before calling. A pass plan is refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` while customers hold access windows that have not run yet — call `publish_plan` with `active=false` instead, which stops new sales while the purchased windows still run. Emits `plan.deleted`. Idempotent — an already-deleted id surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, exactly as an unknown or out-of-scope id does.

plan_id.description: UUID of the plan to delete.

tools.name: delete_payment_method
tools.title: Delete Payment Method
tools.description: Removes a payment method from a project. The row is soft-deleted, so subscriptions sold through it keep their gateway for refunds and history, and configuring the same gateway again later revives it. Requires `project_id` and `payment_method_id`. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `payment_method_id` with a human before calling — buyers lose that way to pay at once. Emits `project.payment_method.deleted`. Idempotent — an already-deleted id surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, exactly as an unknown or out-of-scope id does.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the method belongs to.

payment_method_id.description: UUID of the payment method to remove.

tools.name: delete_coupon
tools.title: Delete Coupon
tools.description: Soft-deletes a coupon code so nobody can redeem it again. Past redemptions and the discounts already applied are kept for history. Requires `coupon_id`. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `coupon_id` with a human before calling. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` while a checkout using the code is still in progress — call `deactivate_coupon` instead, which stops new redemptions immediately without touching the checkout under way. Emits `coupon.deleted`. Idempotent — an already-deleted id surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, exactly as an unknown or out-of-scope id does.

coupon_id.description: UUID of the coupon to delete.

tools.name: delete_canned_reply
tools.title: Delete Canned Reply
tools.description: Removes a saved support reply from a project's picker. Requires `project_id` and `canned_reply_id`. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `canned_reply_id` with a human before calling. Replies already sent with the snippet are untouched. Emits `support.canned_reply.deleted`. Idempotent — an already-deleted id surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, exactly as an unknown or out-of-scope id does.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the snippet belongs to.

canned_reply_id.description: UUID of the saved reply to remove.

tools.name: deactivate_resource
tools.title: Deactivate Resource
tools.description: Switches a project resource off without touching the plans that sell it; switch it back on with `activate_resource`. Requires `resource_id`. Idempotent — re-calling on a resource that is already off is a no-op and emits nothing. Emits `project.resource.updated` when the switch flips. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

resource_id.description: UUID of the resource to switch off.

tools.name: deactivate_payment_method
tools.title: Deactivate Payment Method
tools.description: Stops offering a payment method to new buyers and re-queues the plan sync for its gateway; the subscriptions already sold through it keep renewing. Requires `project_id` and `payment_method_id`. Idempotent — re-calling on a method that is already off is a no-op and emits nothing. Emits `project.payment_method.updated` when the switch flips. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the method belongs to.

payment_method_id.description: UUID of the payment method to switch off.

tools.name: deactivate_coupon
tools.title: Deactivate Coupon
tools.description: Switches a coupon code off so no new subscriber can redeem it. A checkout that already applied the code keeps its discount, which is why this is the right call when a code must stop right away — `delete_coupon` refuses while such a checkout is in progress. Requires `coupon_id`. Idempotent — re-calling on a code that is already off is a no-op. Emits `coupon.deactivated`. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

coupon_id.description: UUID of the coupon to switch off.

tools.name: create_webhook_endpoint
tools.title: Create Webhook Endpoint
tools.description: Registers an outbound webhook endpoint for the token's team. Requires `name`, a public `https` `url` and a non-empty `events` list drawn from `subscriby://enums/webhook-event`; optional `project_id` (deliver only that project's events), `allowed_ips` and `is_active` (default true). The signing secret is returned in this response only, under `secret`, and can never be read again — store it immediately; rotate it later with `rotate_webhook_endpoint_secret`. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` per field, including an http or private-network URL. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope project ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

name.description: A label for the endpoint, shown in the dashboard.

url.description: The https URL Subscriby posts events to. Must resolve to a public address; http and private-network targets are refused.

events.description: Event names to deliver, from subscriby://enums/webhook-event. At least one.

project_id.description: Optional project UUID: deliver only that project's events. Omit for every project of the team.

allowed_ips.description: Optional list of IP addresses or CIDR ranges the endpoint host may resolve to; a delivery whose host resolves outside the list is dead-lettered without being posted.

is_active.description: Whether deliveries start right away. Defaults to true.

tools.name: create_pass_window
tools.title: Create Pass Window
tools.description: Places one dated access window by hand on a time-limited pass plan, marked manual so a schedule rebuild keeps it. Requires `plan_id` (a plan of kind `pass`), `starts_at` (ISO 8601; a value without an offset is read in the plan's own timezone) and `duration_minutes` (a whole number of at least 1; the plan's configured floor and ceiling apply). Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` for a plan that is not a pass, a start in the past, a length outside the bounds or a start the plan already has. Emits `pass.window_scheduled`. Returns the new window in the `get_pass_window` row shape. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope plan ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

plan_id.description: UUID of the pass plan to place the window on.

starts_at.description: ISO 8601 instant the window opens. Without an offset it is read in the plan's own timezone.

duration_minutes.description: How long the window runs, in whole minutes.

tools.name: create_canned_reply
tools.title: Create Canned Reply
tools.description: Saves a reusable support reply on a project. Requires `project_id`, `title` (2..80 chars) and `body` (2..4000 chars); optional `shortcut` (letters, numbers, dashes and underscores, up to 30, unique within the project — the slash-command a creator types to pull the snippet in) and `sort_order` (0..999, the position in the picker). Emits `support.canned_reply.created`. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` per field. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope project ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the snippet belongs to.

title.description: Short label shown in the picker, 2 to 80 characters.

shortcut.description: Slash-command a creator types to insert the snippet: letters, numbers, dashes and underscores, up to 30 characters, unique within the project.

sort_order.description: Position in the picker, 0 to 999. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: cancel_pass_window
tools.title: Cancel Pass Window
tools.description: Cancels one dated access window and resettles everyone holding it. Single-date holders are moved to the plan's next window on sale, or have their pass ended and flagged for a refund when the schedule has nothing left. Season-ticket holders follow `series_holders`: `substitute` (the default) moves them to the next window on sale too, keeping their season at the same length; `drop` removes the cancelled date from their season, leaves the rest standing and reports what the date was worth per holder. Requires `project_id` and `window_id`. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `window_id` and the `series_holders` choice with a human before calling — holders are messaged with the amounts and money may be owed. Emits `pass.window_cancelled`, plus a `pass.holder_moved`, `pass.holder_stranded`, `pass_series.leg_substituted` or `pass_series.leg_dropped` event per holder. Returns the cancelled window row with `meta.rebound`, `meta.refund_due`, `meta.legs_dropped`, `meta.series_holders`, `meta.refunds` (one row per holder owed a decision: the member, the reason, what they paid and what the date was worth, in the holder's own currency) and `meta.refund_totals` per currency; Subscriby never moves the refunds itself. Idempotent — an already-cancelled window is answered with zero tallies. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`; an unknown `series_holders` as `VALIDATION_FAILED`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose pass plans own the window.

window_id.description: UUID of the window to cancel.

series_holders.description: What happens to season-ticket holders of the window: "substitute" (the default) moves them to the plan's next window on sale, keeping their season at the same length; "drop" removes the cancelled date from their season, leaves the rest standing and reports what the date was worth per holder. Single-date holders are always moved where a window is on sale.

tools.name: block_support_contact
tools.title: Block Support Contact
tools.description: Drops every further support message from the member behind a thread; they get no indication they were blocked and cannot reopen the thread by writing again. Requires `conversation_id`. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `conversation_id` with a human before calling — this silences a real person. Their subscription and access are untouched; to remove access call `kick_member` or `ban_member`. Reverse it with `unblock_support_contact`. Emits `support.conversation.blocked` when the block is placed. Idempotent — an already-blocked member is a no-op and emits nothing. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

conversation_id.description: UUID of the support conversation whose member to block.

tools.name: assign_support_conversation
tools.title: Assign Support Conversation
tools.description: Hands a support thread to one team member, or takes it back off everyone. Requires `conversation_id`; `assignee_user_id` is the UUID of the project owner or a member of the project's team, or null to unassign. Any other user is refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Idempotent — assigning the same person again is a no-op. Emits `support.conversation.assigned`. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

conversation_id.description: UUID of the support conversation to assign.

assignee_user_id.description: UUID of the project owner or a team member to hand the thread to. Omit or pass null to unassign.

tools.name: activate_resource
tools.title: Activate Resource
tools.description: Switches a project resource on so the plans that link it grant it again. Requires `resource_id`. Idempotent — re-calling on a resource that is already on is a no-op and emits nothing. Emits `project.resource.updated` when the switch flips. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

resource_id.description: UUID of the resource to switch on.

tools.name: activate_payment_method
tools.title: Activate Payment Method
tools.description: Offers a configured payment method to buyers again and re-queues the plan sync for its gateway. Requires `project_id` and `payment_method_id`. Idempotent — re-calling on a method that is already on is a no-op. A Stripe method whose Connect onboarding never finished is refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED`: it can only be completed from the dashboard. Emits `project.payment_method.updated` when the switch flips. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the method belongs to.

payment_method_id.description: UUID of the payment method to switch on.

tools.name: activate_coupon
tools.title: Activate Coupon
tools.description: Switches a coupon code on so subscribers can redeem it again, subject to its own start date, expiry and redemption cap. Requires `coupon_id`. Idempotent — re-calling on a code that is already on is a no-op. Emits `coupon.activated`. Refused with `TEAM_TIER_REQUIRED` when the project owner's tier no longer includes coupons. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

coupon_id.description: UUID of the coupon to switch on.

tools.name: get_referral_program
tools.title: Get Referral Program
tools.description: Fetches a project's Referral Program by `project_id`: what referrers earn (`free_days` or a `cash` commission with its type, rate, currency and period), what referred friends receive on their first purchase, whether only customers may join and whether the creator approves each affiliate, the hold before a commission is payable, the creator's own terms and the plans a conversion counts on (`plan_ids` empty means EVERY plan). Same flat keys as `update_referral_program` takes. A project with no programme, an unknown project or one outside the token's scope surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose Referral Program to fetch.

tools.name: update_referral_program
tools.title: Update Referral Program
tools.description: Sets up or changes a project's Referral Program; the first call on a project creates it, every later call changes only the arguments present. Requires `project_id`. Optional: `active`, `customers_only`, `approval_required`, `reward_kind` (`free_days` or `cash`), `reward_days` (1..3650, for free days), `commission_type` (`percentage` or `fixed`, for cash), `commission_value` (0.0001..100 for a percentage, any amount above zero for a fixed commission), `commission_currency_id` (needed for a fixed commission), `commission_period_months` (0 for the friend's first payment only, 1..36, or null for life), `hold_days` (0..90), `minimum_payout` (a guide only, null for none), `friend_reward_kind` (`none`, `free_days` or `coupon`), `friend_reward_days`, `friend_coupon_id` (one of the project's coupons), `payout_details_label`, `terms` and `plan_ids` (an empty list counts conversions on every plan, including ones added later). Rewards already in the ledger keep their figures, and every approved or pending affiliate is told in their chat and by mail when a field they were promised moves. Emits `referral.program_updated`. Refused with `TEAM_TIER_REQUIRED` when the project owner's plan does not include the Referral Program, with `VALIDATION_FAILED` when a field is invalid or the shape does not add up.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose Referral Program to set up or change.

active.description: The on/off switch. Prefer activate_referral_program and deactivate_referral_program, which change only this.

customers_only.description: Whether only members with a live membership may join.

approval_required.description: Whether the creator approves each affiliate before their code counts.

reward_kind.description: "free_days" (membership days banked on the referrer) or "cash" (a commission the creator pays out themselves).

reward_days.description: Days a referrer earns per converted friend, 1..3650; for a free_days reward.

commission_type.description: "percentage" of every settled payment or a "fixed" amount on the first; for a cash reward.

commission_value.description: The rate: 0.0001..100 for a percentage, any amount above zero for a fixed commission.

commission_currency_id.description: Currency UUID a fixed commission is paid in; ignored and cleared for a percentage.

commission_period_months.description: How long a percentage commission runs after conversion: 0 for the friend's first payment only, 1..36 months, or null for life.

hold_days.description: Days a cash commission waits before it is payable, 0..90.

minimum_payout.description: A guide for the creator, the balance an affiliate reaches before they pay; nothing is enforced. Pass null for none.

friend_reward_kind.description: What a referred friend receives on their first purchase: "none", "free_days" or "coupon".

friend_reward_days.description: Days banked on the friend's first purchase, 1..3650; for a free_days friend reward.

friend_coupon_id.description: UUID of one of the project's coupon codes, applied at the friend's checkout; for a coupon friend reward.

payout_details_label.description: The question affiliates answer so the creator can pay them, such as "PayPal email"; at most 120 characters, null for none.

terms.description: The creator's own terms, shown to affiliates and referred friends; at most 5,000 characters, null for none.

plan_ids.description: Plan UUIDs a conversion must be on to count. An empty list counts every plan in the project, including ones added later.

tools.name: activate_referral_program
tools.title: Activate Referral Program
tools.description: Switches a project's Referral Program on: affiliates' links and codes attribute again and settled payments earn again, and every affiliate is told the terms as they now stand. Requires `project_id`. Idempotent: a programme already on is left as it is and nothing is emitted. Emits `referral.program_updated` with `active` as the one change. Refused with `TEAM_TIER_REQUIRED` when the project owner's plan does not include the Referral Program; a project with no programme surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose Referral Program to switch on.

tools.name: deactivate_referral_program
tools.title: Deactivate Referral Program
tools.description: Switches a project's Referral Program off: links and codes stop attributing and settled payments stop earning at once, while what affiliates already earned stays and can still be paid out. Every affiliate is told their link no longer counts new friends. Requires `project_id`. Idempotent: a programme already off is left as it is and nothing is emitted. Emits `referral.program_updated` with `active` as the one change. A project with no programme surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose Referral Program to switch off.

tools.name: delete_referral_program
tools.title: Delete Referral Program
tools.description: Removes a project's Referral Program. Requires `project_id`. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `project_id` with a human before calling. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` while any affiliate is still owed a commission; record their payouts with `record_referral_payout`, or call `deactivate_referral_program` instead, which stops the programme and keeps everything. Deleting emits no event. Idempotent: a project with no programme surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, exactly as an unknown or out-of-scope project does.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose Referral Program to remove.

tools.name: list_referral_affiliates
tools.title: List Referral Affiliates
tools.description: Lists the members enrolled in a project's Referral Program, newest first. Requires `project_id`; optional `status` (`pending`, `approved` or `suspended`) and `member_id` to find one member's affiliate row. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page` (default 1). A list row carries the code, status and days balance but never the per-currency balances; call `get_referral_affiliate` for what one affiliate is owed. Payout details an affiliate typed are never surfaced by any tool.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose affiliates to list.

member_id.description: Optional member UUID, to find that member's affiliate row.

limit.description: Maximum affiliates to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: get_referral_affiliate
tools.title: Get Referral Affiliate
tools.description: Fetches one affiliate of a project's Referral Program by `project_id` and `affiliate_id`, with their code, status, days balance and `balances` per currency: `pending` (inside the hold), `earned`, `payable` (what `record_referral_payout` may record) and `paid_out`, each a decimal string. Same row as `list_referral_affiliates` plus the balances. The payout details they typed are never surfaced. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the affiliate belongs to.

affiliate_id.description: UUID of the affiliate to fetch.

tools.name: add_referral_affiliate
tools.title: Add Referral Affiliate
tools.description: Enrols a member of a project as an affiliate of its Referral Program by hand, approved whatever the programme's customers-only and approval switches say, and hands them their code, their links and the programme's terms in their chat and by mail. Requires `project_id` and `member_id` (a member of that project, as `list_subscribers` lists them). Emits `referral.affiliate_joined`. Refused with `TEAM_TIER_REQUIRED` when the project owner's plan does not include the Referral Program, with `VALIDATION_FAILED` when the member already stands in the programme, and with `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` for a project with no programme or a member not of the project.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose Referral Program the member joins.

member_id.description: UUID of the member to enrol, as list_subscribers lists them.

tools.name: approve_referral_affiliate
tools.title: Approve Referral Affiliate
tools.description: Approves a pending or suspended affiliate of a project's Referral Program: their code counts from now on, and they receive their link, code and the programme's terms in their chat and by mail. Requires `project_id` and `affiliate_id`. Idempotent: an affiliate already approved is left as they are and nothing is emitted. Emits `referral.affiliate_approved`. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the affiliate belongs to.

affiliate_id.description: UUID of the affiliate to approve.

tools.name: suspend_referral_affiliate
tools.title: Suspend Referral Affiliate
tools.description: Suspends an affiliate of a project's Referral Program: their code stops counting new friends and nothing new is earned, while what they already earned stays and can still be paid out. Requires `project_id` and `affiliate_id`. DESTRUCTIVE: a real person stops earning, so confirm the target with a human before calling. Idempotent: an affiliate already suspended is left as they are and nothing is emitted. Emits `referral.affiliate_suspended`. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the affiliate belongs to.

affiliate_id.description: UUID of the affiliate to suspend.

tools.name: list_referrals
tools.title: List Referrals
tools.description: Lists the friends affiliates of a project's Referral Program brought in, newest first: how each arrived (`source` is `portal_link`, `connector_link` or `code_at_checkout`), whether their first payment settled (`status` is `touched`, `converted`, `expired` or `rejected`) and until when the affiliate earns on them. Requires `project_id`; optional `status`, `affiliate_id` and `since` (an ISO 8601 instant: only referrals whose friend arrived on or after it, so a report can page what happened since its last run). Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page` (default 1). Nothing names a friend beyond their member id.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose referrals to list.

affiliate_id.description: Optional affiliate UUID, to list one affiliate's referrals.

since.description: Optional ISO 8601 instant: only referrals whose friend arrived on or after it.

limit.description: Maximum referrals to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: get_referral
tools.title: Get Referral
tools.description: Fetches one referral of a project's Referral Program by `project_id` and `referral_id`: the affiliate, the friend's member id, how they arrived, whether their first payment settled and until when the affiliate earns on them. Same row shape as `list_referrals`. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the referral belongs to.

referral_id.description: UUID of the referral to fetch.

tools.name: list_referral_rewards
tools.title: List Referral Rewards
tools.description: Lists the referral ledger of a project, newest first: one row per settled payment per side of a referral, with the days or money it earned, whose it is (`beneficiary` is `referrer` or `friend`) and where it stands (`status` is `pending` inside the hold, `approved` payable, `paid`, `applied` for days banked on a membership, or `reversed` by a refund; a reversal is its own row with a negative amount). Requires `project_id`; optional `affiliate_id`, `status` and `beneficiary`. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page` (default 1). Read-only: nothing here is written by hand.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose referral ledger to list.

affiliate_id.description: Optional affiliate UUID, to list one affiliate's rewards.

limit.description: Maximum rewards to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_referral_payouts
tools.title: List Referral Payouts
tools.description: Lists the payouts recorded against a project's affiliates, newest first: how much the creator paid each affiliate outside Subscriby, in which currency, the creator's reference and note, and how many payable commissions the payout covered. Requires `project_id`; optional `affiliate_id`. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page` (default 1).

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose payouts to list.

affiliate_id.description: Optional affiliate UUID, to list one affiliate's payouts.

limit.description: Maximum payouts to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: record_referral_payout
tools.title: Record Referral Payout
tools.description: Records a payout the creator made to an affiliate outside Subscriby, so the ledger marks their oldest payable commissions in that currency as paid, first in first out, until the amount is covered. Requires `project_id`, `affiliate_id`, `amount` (greater than zero) and `currency_id`; optional `reference` (at most 120 characters) and `note` (at most 1,000). DESTRUCTIVE: it records that money left and emits `referral.payout_recorded`, so read the affiliate's `balances` with `get_referral_affiliate` first and confirm with a human. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` when the amount exceeds the payable balance in that currency (`error.context.balance` carries what is payable) or the currency is unknown; an affiliate not of the project surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the affiliate belongs to.

affiliate_id.description: UUID of the affiliate who was paid.

amount.description: What was paid, greater than zero and at most the affiliate's payable balance in the currency.

currency_id.description: UUID of the currency the commissions were earned in; a balance exists per currency.

reference.description: The creator's own reference, such as a transfer id; at most 120 characters.

note.description: A note for the creator's records; at most 1,000 characters.

tools.name: get_partner_program
tools.title: Get Partner Program
tools.description: Describes where the creator this token belongs to stands in the Partner Program, Subscriby's own programme where a creator earns a share of every invoice paid by the creators they bring to Subscriby: the `status` (`applied` under review, `active`, `rejected` with `reapply_available_at`, `suspended`), and once approved the partner `code`, the `links` to hand out (the web link and one deep link per connector), the commission ladder (`commission_percent` now, `base_percent`, `max_percent`, the commitment and volume points, `paying_referrals` and the next volume tier), the referral tallies by state, the `balance` (pending, payable, credited, paid, earned, decimal strings in USD), the `payout_method` with `payout_details_complete` (the destination itself is never returned), the tax declaration, the terms acceptance and every promotion commitment with its proof state. Takes no input. Applying is done on the dashboard or in the bot: a creator who never applied surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

tools.name: list_partner_referrals
tools.title: List Partner Referrals
tools.description: Lists the creators the token's creator brought to Subscriby as a partner, newest first: each with the referred creator's display name (never their email or id), how they arrived (`source` is `link`, `code_at_signup` or `bot_deep_link`), whether their first paid invoice converted them (`status` is `signed_up`, `converted`, `under_review`, `expired` or `rejected`), the plan they converted on, the rate locked onto them and until when the partner earns on them. Optional `status`. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page` (default 1). A creator who never applied to the programme surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

limit.description: Maximum referrals to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_partner_rewards
tools.title: List Partner Rewards
tools.description: Lists the token's creator's Partner Program commission ledger, newest first: one row per paid invoice of a creator they referred (`kind` is `commission`), priced from the invoice's total before tax and after discount (`base_amount`) at the referral's locked rate (`amount`, a decimal string in USD), plus the clawbacks that answer a reversal of money already settled (`kind` is `clawback`, a negative `amount`). `status` is `pending` (inside the hold), `approved` (payable), `credited` (applied as Subscriby Credit), `paid` (covered by a cash payout) or `reversed`; `note` says why a row was reversed or re-priced. Optional `status`. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page` (default 1). A creator who never applied to the programme surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_partner_payouts
tools.title: List Partner Payouts
tools.description: Lists the cash payouts Subscriby made to the token's creator as a partner, newest first: the `amount` (a decimal string in USD), the rail the money went by (`method` is `paypal`, `wise`, `remitly` or `crypto`), the transfer's `reference`, when it left and how many commissions it covered (`rewards_paid`). Commissions settled as Subscriby Credit are not payouts; read them on `list_partner_rewards` as `credited`. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page` (default 1). A creator who never applied to the programme surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

limit.description: Maximum payouts to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: update_partner_payout_details
tools.title: Update Partner Payout Details
tools.description: Writes how the token's creator is paid as a partner: `method` (`credit` for Subscriby Credit on their own invoices while that rail is open, `paypal`, `wise`, `remitly` or `crypto` for USDT on TRC20), `details` (the PayPal email or the wallet address, for `paypal` and `crypto`), the bank account for `wise` and `remitly` (`bank_holder`, `bank_name`, `bank_country`, `bank_account_number`, optional `bank_swift`, `bank_branch_code`, `bank_address`), the tax declaration every cash rail needs (`legal_name`, `tax_country`, optional `us_person`) and `accept_terms` (true to accept the Partner Program Terms with this save; a rail cannot be saved until they are accepted). Only the destination the chosen rail uses is kept, encrypted; no tool ever returns it. Answers the partner object as `get_partner_program` describes it. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` when a field is invalid, the terms are not accepted, the credit rail is closed, the detail or the account is missing, or the application is not yet approved; with `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` when the creator never applied. Emits no event.

details.description: The PayPal email for "paypal" or the USDT TRC20 wallet address for "crypto"; at most 190 characters. Ignored on the other rails.

bank_holder.description: The name on the bank account, for "wise" and "remitly"; at most 120 characters.

bank_name.description: The bank, for "wise" and "remitly"; at most 120 characters.

bank_country.description: Where the bank is, as a two-letter ISO country code, for "wise" and "remitly".

bank_account_number.description: The account number or IBAN, for "wise" and "remitly": letters, digits, spaces and dashes, at most 40 characters.

bank_swift.description: Optional SWIFT or BIC code, 8 or 11 characters.

bank_branch_code.description: Optional branch, routing, sort or IFSC code: letters, digits, spaces and dashes, at most 20 characters.

bank_address.description: Optional account holder's address, at most 200 characters.

legal_name.description: The name a payment is made out to; required on every cash rail, at most 120 characters.

tax_country.description: The country of tax residence, as a two-letter ISO country code; required on every cash rail.

us_person.description: Whether the creator is a US person for tax purposes.

accept_terms.description: True to accept the Partner Program Terms with this save.

tools.name: accept_partner_terms
tools.title: Accept Partner Terms
tools.description: Records that the token's creator accepts the Partner Program Terms as they stand today, which every payout rail requires; accepting again after the terms change is the same call. Answers the partner object as `get_partner_program` describes it, with `terms_accepted_at` and `terms_version` set. Takes no input. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` while the application is under review or was declined, and with `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` when the creator never applied. Emits no event.

tools.name: list_transaction_fees
tools.title: List Transaction Fees
tools.description: Lists the transaction fees Subscriby charged the creator this token belongs to, newest first, one row per fee: `kind` says what it was for (`payment_fee`, the commission on a member's payment; `access_code_fee`, a code redeemed past the plan's free allotment; `trial_usage`, the metered fees a platform trial waived, collected once it ended; `outage_emails`, emails sent to members during a recovery; `processing_recovery`, the cost of collecting an invoice's fee lines), `channel` how it was collected ("connect_at_source", deducted from the member's payment by Stripe Connect and never invoiced, or "metered", reported to the usage meter and billed on the creator's own Subscriby invoice), and each row carries the project, the member and the payment where there was one, the gross amount and the rate, `fee_amount` as a decimal string in the creator's billing currency, the meter `units`, and `invoice_id` with `invoiced_at` once a paid Subscriby invoice billed a metered line. Optional `month` (`YYYY-MM`, UTC; wins over the bounds), `from` and `to` (ISO 8601), `project_id`, `channel` and `kind`. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page` (default 1).

month.description: Optional calendar month as "YYYY-MM" in UTC, such as "2026-10"; wins over from and to.

from.description: Optional lower bound, ISO 8601: lines incurred at or after it.

to.description: Optional upper bound, ISO 8601: lines incurred before it.

project_id.description: Optional project id: only the lines earned on that project.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: get_transaction_fee_summary
tools.title: Get Transaction Fee Summary
tools.description: Adds up one calendar month of the transaction fees Subscriby charged the creator this token belongs to: `total_fee`, `at_source_fee` (deducted from members' payments by Stripe Connect, never invoiced), `metered_fee` (reported to the usage meter and billed on the creator's own Subscriby invoice; the figure to hold against the invoice's Transaction Fees line) with `metered_units`, `invoiced_fee` and `awaiting_invoice_fee`, every amount a decimal string in the creator's billing currency, plus `by_kind` (one row per kind of fee with its label, sum, units and line count), `by_project` (largest first; the fees no project carries pool under a null id) and `invoices` (the Subscriby invoices that billed the month's metered lines, newest first). Optional `month` (`YYYY-MM`, UTC; the current month by default) and `project_id` (one project alone, in which case `by_project` is empty).

month.description: Optional calendar month as "YYYY-MM" in UTC, such as "2026-10"; the current month when left out.

project_id.description: Optional project id: add up that project's lines alone.

tools.name: list_knowledge_entries
tools.title: List Knowledge Entries
tools.description: Lists what a project has taught Subscriby Copilot, newest first: every Knowledge entry with its "kind" ("question" or "document"), its "audience" ("members" may be answered from it, "team" serves the creator's own surfaces alone), its "status" ("ready", "indexing" or "failed"), its title and how many passages it became. The rows carry no text; `get_knowledge_entry` does. Requires `project_id`; optional `limit` (1..100) and `page`. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose Knowledge to list.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: get_knowledge_entry
tools.title: Get Knowledge Entry
tools.description: Reads one Knowledge entry of a project with its text: the question and its answer, or the document's name and its words, plus "kind", "audience", "status", how many passages it became and when it was last indexed. Requires `project_id` and `knowledge_entry_id`. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the entry belongs to.

tools.name: create_knowledge_entry
tools.title: Create Knowledge Entry
tools.description: Teaches Subscriby Copilot something about a project: a question with its answer, or a document sent as text, cut into passages and indexed the moment it is saved. Requires `project_id`, `kind` ("question" or "document"), `title` (the question or the document's name, 2..160 chars) and `body` (the answer or the document's text, 2..50000 chars; a Markdown document keeps its headings); optional `audience` ("members", the default, lets members be answered from it in the inbox, the bot and the portal; "team" keeps it to the creator's own surfaces). A project holds at most 200 entries. Emits `knowledge.created`. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` per field. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project to teach.

kind.description: "question" for a question with its answer, "document" for a plain-text or Markdown guide sent as text.

title.description: The question, worded the way a member asks it, or the document's name; 2 to 160 characters.

body.description: The answer, or the document's text; 2 to 50000 characters, facts only.

audience.description: "members" (the default) lets members be answered from the entry; "team" keeps it to the creator's own surfaces.

tools.name: update_knowledge_entry
tools.title: Update Knowledge Entry
tools.description: Changes a Knowledge entry; anything you omit keeps its stored value and the kind never changes. Requires `project_id` and `knowledge_entry_id`. Optional: `title` (2..160 chars), `body` (2..50000 chars; new words are cut into passages again in the same step) and `audience` ("members" or "team"; a change retags the passages without rewriting them). Emits `knowledge.updated` with the changed fields when something moved. Refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` per field. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the entry belongs to.

knowledge_entry_id.description: UUID of the entry to change, from `list_knowledge_entries`.

title.description: The question, or the document's name; 2 to 160 characters.

body.description: The answer, or the document's text; 2 to 50000 characters. New words are cut into passages again.

audience.description: "members" lets members be answered from the entry; "team" keeps it to the creator's own surfaces.

tools.name: delete_knowledge_entry
tools.title: Delete Knowledge Entry
tools.description: Removes a Knowledge entry from a project with its passages and its file, so the Copilot stops answering from it at once. Requires `project_id` and `knowledge_entry_id`. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `knowledge_entry_id` with the creator before calling; read it back with `get_knowledge_entry` first. Emits `knowledge.deleted`. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the entry belongs to.

knowledge_entry_id.description: UUID of the entry to remove, from `list_knowledge_entries`.

tools.name: get_copilot_credits
tools.title: Get Copilot Credits
tools.description: Describes the Copilot Credits of the creator this token belongs to, in one object: `balance` (`total_cents`, `free_cents` spent first, `paid_cents` which never lapses, `lapsing_cents` with `lapsing_at`, `exhausted`), `allowance` (this month's free operator turns and member answers, used and left), this month's `turns_this_month`, `suggestions_this_month`, `answers_this_month` and `paid_spent_this_month_cents`, the prices (`price_turn_cents`, `price_suggestion_cents`, `price_answer_cents`, with `long_turn_steps` and `max_turn_steps`), `low_balance_cents`, the `packs` on sale and the `settings` (auto top-up and monthly cap). Every amount is an integer in US cents. Takes no input; requires `account:read`.

tools.name: list_copilot_credits_statement
tools.title: List Copilot Credits Statement
tools.description: Pages the Copilot Credits statement of the creator this token belongs to, newest first: every pack bought and its bonus, every promotion and goodwill grant, every refund and lapse, and each month's usage per kind, each line with its `kind`, `cents` (positive for credit, negative for debit), `at`, `label`, `expires_at` on a free grant, and `units` with `usage_kind` on a usage line. Optional `limit` (1..100) and `page`. Requires `account:read`.

limit.description: Maximum lines to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: create_copilot_credits_pack
tools.title: Create Copilot Credits Pack
tools.description: Opens the purchase of a pack of Copilot Credits for the creator this token belongs to and answers the Stripe Checkout URL to send them to, with the pack's `paid_cents` and `bonus_cents`; nothing is charged and no credit lands until the creator pays on that page, and the card they pay with is saved for the auto top-up. Requires `pack`, one of the packs `get_copilot_credits` lists on sale ("starter", "regular", "plus" or "max"); a pack with no price in this environment is refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Requires `account:write`.

pack.description: The pack to buy: "starter" ($10), "regular" ($25 with $2.50 free), "plus" ($50 with $7.50 free) or "max" ($100 with $15 free).

tools.name: update_copilot_credits_settings
tools.title: Update Copilot Credits Settings
tools.description: Changes the Copilot Credits settings of the creator this token belongs to; anything you omit keeps its stored value. Optional: `auto_topup_pack` (one of the packs on sale, "starter", "regular", "plus" or "max"; null switches the auto top-up off; switching it on needs a card on file, else `VALIDATION_FAILED`), `auto_topup_below_cents` (100..10000, the balance under which the auto top-up buys) and `monthly_spend_cap_cents` (0..1000000, the paid credit the Copilot may draw in a calendar month; the free allowance is never capped). Answers the settings after the change. Requires `account:write`.

auto_topup_pack.description: The pack the auto top-up buys: "starter", "regular", "plus" or "max"; null switches the auto top-up off.

auto_topup_below_cents.description: The balance in US cents under which the auto top-up buys (100..10000).

monthly_spend_cap_cents.description: The paid credit in US cents the Copilot may draw in a calendar month (0..1000000).

tools.name: get_group
tools.title: Get Group
tools.description: Fetches one group by UUID: its team, code and name. Same row shape as `list_groups`. Groups cluster users for organization but carry no permission payload of their own. Unknown ids and groups of teams the caller does not belong to surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

group_id.description: UUID of the group to fetch.

tools.name: get_role
tools.title: Get Role
tools.description: Fetches one role by UUID: its team, code, name and the permission codes it grants. Same row shape as `list_roles`. Unknown ids and roles of teams the caller does not belong to surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

role_id.description: UUID of the role to fetch.

tools.name: get_team_member
tools.title: Get Team Member
tools.description: Fetches one member of a team by the member's user UUID: their name, email, role and whether they own the team. Same row shape as `list_team_members`. Requires `team_id` and `member_id`. A team the caller does not belong to, and a user who is not on the team, both surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

team_id.description: UUID of the team the member is on.

tools.name: get_token
tools.title: Get Personal Access Token
tools.description: Fetches one of the authenticated user's own personal access tokens by UUID: its name, gate abilities, team and project scopes, last use and expiry. Same row shape as `list_tokens`; the plaintext value is NEVER surfaced — it exists only in the mint's own answer. Unknown ids and other users' tokens surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

token_id.description: UUID of the token to fetch, from `list_tokens`.

tools.name: create_token
tools.title: Create Personal Access Token
tools.description: Mints a personal access token: a `name`, the `abilities` it holds (each a value from the ability catalog, and never more than the calling token itself holds — "token:create" is refused unconditionally), and the `team_id` it is minted for, which must be a team the caller owns or belongs to and becomes the token's frozen scope. The answer carries the token row plus `token`, the plaintext, THE ONLY TIME IT EXISTS outside your own storage — hand it to the person or store it immediately; every later read returns the row without it. A refused ability or a foreign team is `VALIDATION_FAILED` naming the reason.

name.description: A label for the token, up to 255 characters, shown on Settings under API Tokens.

abilities.description: The abilities the token holds, at least one, each a value from the ability catalog resource. Must be a subset of what the calling token holds; "token:create" is never granted this way.

team_id.description: UUID of the team the token is minted for; it becomes the token's frozen scope and must be a team the caller owns or belongs to.

tools.name: get_alert_destinations
tools.title: Get Alert Destinations
tools.description: Lists where the authenticated creator's alerts go: each destination's kind ("connector_identity" or "email"), target, the alert classes routed to it (null means every class, an empty list means none), whether it is the primary connected account, and when it was verified. The same rows Settings or Notifications edits and `GET /v1/me/alert-destinations` returns. Takes no arguments; `get_me` carries the matching "alert_destinations_default" flag.

tools.name: update_alert_destinations
tools.title: Update Alert Destinations
tools.description: Replaces the full set of places the authenticated creator's alerts go. Pass "destinations" as the complete wanted list (max 20) — rows left out are removed, an empty list silences everything. Each row: "kind" ("connector_identity" or "email"), "target" (the connected account's id from `get_me`'s identities, or an email address), and optional "classes" (any of the alert class words; omit or null for every class, an empty list keeps the destination but routes nothing). A target that is not one of the caller's own accounts or addresses is `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`; an unknown kind or class is `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Answers the destinations as they now stand, the same rows `get_alert_destinations` reads.

destinations.description: The complete wanted list of destinations, at most 20: objects of "kind" ("connector_identity" or "email"), "target", and optional "classes" (alert class words; omit for every class, empty list for none). Rows left out are removed.

tools.name: get_partner_referral
tools.title: Get Partner Referral
tools.description: Fetches one of the authenticated partner's referrals by UUID: who signed up through the link or code, its status, the conversion window and what the conversion earned. Same row shape as `list_partner_referrals`. A creator who never applied for the Partner Program, and a referral of another partner, both surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

referral_id.description: UUID of the referral to fetch, from `list_partner_referrals`.

tools.name: get_recovery_incident
tools.title: Get Recovery Incident
tools.description: Fetches one Disaster Recovery incident by UUID: what the probes found, the installation or resource it concerns, when it was detected and whether it has closed. Same row shape as `list_recovery_incidents`. Unknown ids and another creator's incidents surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

incident_id.description: UUID of the incident to fetch, from `list_recovery_incidents`.

tools.name: get_recovery_operation
tools.title: Get Recovery Operation
tools.description: Fetches one Disaster Recovery operation by UUID: its kind, status, what it moved or replaced, the readmission tallies and when it ran. Same row shape as `list_recovery_operations`. Read it before `revert_recovery_operation` or `nudge_pending_readmissions` to see the current state rather than assuming it; `get_recovery_roll_call` lists the members it readmitted. Unknown ids and another creator's operations surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

operation_id.description: UUID of the operation to fetch, from `list_recovery_operations`.

tools.name: list_broadcast_audiences
tools.title: List Broadcast Audiences
tools.description: Lists every audience segment `broadcast_message` accepts for a project: the segment's value and label, what it means, whether it requires a pass window, whether it can be narrowed to a plan, whether it reads the expiring-within-days horizon, and a recipient estimate (null for segments that need a pass window first). Call it before composing a broadcast; `preview_broadcast_audience` sizes one segment with your exact filters. Requires `project_id`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the broadcast would go to.

tools.name: list_subscriptions
tools.title: List Subscriptions
tools.description: Pages every subscription the token may see, newest first: id, plan, subscriber, payment method, payment status, price, trial end, end date and whether it was cancelled — the same row shape `get_subscription` answers, which adds the access grants. Optional "status" matches one payment status ("trialing", "active", "incomplete", "expired", "past_due", "canceled", "unpaid", "paused", "processing", "succeeded", "capturable" or "failed"; an unknown word is `VALIDATION_FAILED`), "plan_id" scopes to one plan, and `limit` (1..100, default 25) with `page` walk the pages. `list_subscribers` lists the people; this lists their purchases.

status.description: Match one payment status word; an unknown value is refused naming the accepted list.

plan_id.description: Scope to one plan by UUID.

limit.description: Rows per page, 1..100. Defaults to 25.

tools.name: revoke_access_code
tools.title: Revoke Access Code
tools.description: Revokes one unredeemed access code by UUID so it can no longer be redeemed and stops appearing in `list_access_codes`. Requires `plan_id` and `access_code_id`. Only a pending, unredeemed code can be revoked: a code that was already redeemed became a subscription and surfaces here as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` — read it through `get_subscription` and cancel it there if that is what you mean to do. Answers the revoked code's id with "revoked" true.

plan_id.description: UUID of the plan the code belongs to.

access_code_id.description: UUID of the unredeemed code, from `list_access_codes`.

resources.name: api-ability-catalog
resources.title: API Ability Catalog
resources.description: Every ability a Sanctum personal access token can carry — core CRUD gates plus top-level scopes for team, role, group, token, payment, pass-window, support-canned-reply, webhook-endpoint, webhook-delivery, broadcast, bot, account, billing, dashboard, activity, platform admin and distribution. MCP and REST answer to the same catalog: a tool requires the same ability its REST equivalent does, so mint for the operations you intend to call rather than for the channel. Read once at session start to know what the current token can do and to mint future tokens with the minimum-privilege list. Returns `{ abilities: [{value, category, label}], core_count, extras_count, total }`.

resources.name: api-error-code-catalog
resources.title: API Error Code Catalog
resources.description: Every error code the API surface and MCP tools can emit. Each entry carries HTTP status, default message, remediation hint, and a docs_url anchor. Read this whenever a tool response carries an `error` envelope so the agent can pick the right remediation before retrying. Returns `{ error_codes: [{code, http_status, message, remediation, docs_url}] }`.

resources.name: connector-catalog
resources.title: Connector Catalog
resources.description: Every connector Subscriby knows, lane by lane: `status` (`available`, `beta`, `paused`, `in_development`, `coming_soon`), `installable`, `official`, badges, category, tagline, links and, for a connector that exists as a package, its manifest (resource kinds with their grant mode, capabilities, messaging limits, pacing, the management commands it renders and the ones it misses, recovery facets) and the declarative install and settings fields a client renders as the connect form. Read this before proposing a connector for a project or explaining what one can do. Returns `{ connectors: [card], total }`.

resources.name: payment-provider-enum
resources.title: Payment Providers
resources.description: The payment-provider keys Subscriby supports: the gateway codes (Stripe, PayPal, Polar, Mollie, Kelviq, Skrill, CoinPayments, Paystack, Razorpay, CeyPay), access codes, and one `connector:provider` key per native currency a connector brings, which can only be configured on a project where that connector is connected. Most flows use payment-method UUIDs from `list_payment_methods` rather than provider codes; consult this resource only when you need the canonical provider string. Returns `{ payment_providers: [{value, connector, requires_connector, legacy_alias}] }`; `platformcurrency` is the legacy alias earlier native rows were stored under.

resources.name: subscription-status-enum
resources.title: Subscription Status Catalog
resources.description: Every status a subscription or payment row can hold, with the human label and the dashboard color family. Read this before reasoning about lifecycle — e.g. is `past_due` a dunning trigger, is `capturable` retryable, is `canceled` terminal? Avoids hard-coding free-text status strings on the agent side. Returns `{ subscription_statuses: [{value, label, color}] }`.

resources.name: webhook-event-catalog
resources.title: Outbound Webhook Event Catalog
resources.description: Every outbound webhook event Subscriby can emit, grouped by family (project, plan, member, subscription, payment, access-code, etc.). Each row carries the minimum ability a subscribing creator must hold to receive that event. Read this before configuring a webhook endpoint or wiring up an external automation (Zapier, n8n) so the event allow-list lines up with the events the source actions actually produce. Returns `{ webhook_events: [{name, family, required_ability}], families: [string] }`.
